records.title: Found by: loop assessment (L19).
records.description: Found by: loop assessment (L19). The result contract had no way to tell our own limits from the server's: scan-static recorded every permanent skip, its own unsupported languages, multi-server layouts, reader limits and reader errors included, as `no_runnable_artifact`, which reads as the subject's. In the first 50 live results, 16 were skips and most were ours. Skips may now carry `fault` (tool, subject, infra, policy); our limits have their own reasons (`unsupported_language`, `unsupported_layout`, `reader_limit`, `no_tools_found`, `too_large`, `tool_error`) that may only be the tool's; a skip without `fault` is read through a fixed map, with `unknown` for an ambiguous reason, never the subject.

records.title: An ingest artifact that failed a check that never changes (a file that is not age, a 0-byte file, an entry past the 1 GiB unzip cap, an entry named `.artifact.json`, or the `.tmp-<pid>` file `ingest/…
records.description: An ingest artifact that failed a check that never changes (a file that is not age, a 0-byte file, an entry past the 1 GiB unzip cap, an entry named `.artifact.json`, or the `.tmp-<pid>` file `ingest/collect.mjs` leaves when the pump is cancelled, which the upload keeps because it runs under `always()`) was refused on every run until GitHub expired it, throwing away the only copy of its results along with every good sealed file beside the bad one. The download is now kept as it came, still encrypted, in `quarantine/<id>-<name>.zip` with a reason file; the files that pass are archived as usual; the index and manifest mark it `partial` with the refused files. Only a download in doubt (digest or size mismatch) is retried.

test.name: R-ARC-04: an ingest artifact with files that will never pass is quarantined as downloaded, its sealed files kept, marked partial, and not retried
R-ARC-04: an ingest zip past the inflated-size cap keeps the entries within it and quarantines the download
R-ARC-04: an unreadable ingest zip is quarantined whole, with no folder, and indexed as partial
R-ARC-04: a partial artifact left in its folder by a run that died is recovered without a second quarantine copy
R-ARC-04: a download in doubt (digest or size mismatch) is retried, not quarantined
R-ARC-04: readZipLenient refuses bad entries one by one and keeps the rest

records.description: Nothing said when the archive pull stopped running or kept failing: its only output was a log file on the Mac. A successful run writes `.last-ok.json` and sets the repository variable `ARCHIVE_LAST_OK` (time and counts) for a remote freshness check.

test.name: R-ARC-05: a failed run shows a notification, and says when the last good run was once that is over a day old
R-ARC-05: a successful run records .last-ok.json and sets ARCHIVE_LAST_OK to the time and the counts
R-ARC-05: a run that quarantines an artifact exits 0, sets the heartbeat and shows a notification
R-ARC-05: a heartbeat that cannot be set is logged and notified, and the run still exits 0
R-ARC-05: no notification and no heartbeat in CI, on a dry run, or when turned off

records.description: An artifact listed twice (the list shifts while it is paged) was pulled once and then "recovered" from its own folder, giving two index lines, because the in-memory index was not updated after an append. records.description: A folder with an artifact's marker, left by an earlier run, was indexed without checking its files, so a damaged or half-synced folder was trusted for good; files were also not synced to disk before the rename. A recovered folder is now re-hashed against its marker (a bad one is left alone and the artifact pulled again under the next name), and every file and folder is fsynced before the rename.

records.title: Two pulls into one archive at the same time (the agent and one started by hand) were not guarded against.
records.description: Two pulls into one archive at the same time (the agent and one started by hand) were not guarded against. A run now holds a `mkdir` lock in `<dest>/.lock`, exits 0 if a live run holds it, and takes over a lock whose pid is gone or that is over 12 hours old. The 12-hour rule for a lock on the same host was later superseded by R-ARC-12 (pid only on this host; 12 hours untouched only for another host's lock).

R-ARC-08: a lock from a dead run on this host, or from another host untouched for 12 hours, is taken over; a recent one from another host is not
R-ARC-08: the lock is released when a run fails part way

records.title: NIT.
records.description: NIT. The `created_at ... is not a date` message never fired: `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` threw its own RangeError first. The time is now checked before it is formatted, and a bad time never becomes the cursor.

test.name: R-ARC-10: an ingest artifact whose created_at is not a date fails with that message

records.title: The inflated-size cap of `readZipLenient` did not bound the work: an entry was counted only after it passed, so entries that inflated and then failed their CRC cost a full inflate each, and many cent…
records.description: The inflated-size cap of `readZipLenient` did not bound the work: an entry was counted only after it passed, so entries that inflated and then failed their CRC cost a full inflate each, and many central-directory entries could point at the same local data. A 67 KB zip of 30 bad-CRC 64 MiB entries inflated 1.88 GiB under a 100 MB cap, reachable through an artifact a fork's pull request uploads. Every entry read now counts before it is inflated, pass or fail, and a local offset used twice is refused.

test.name: R-ARC-11: entries that fail after inflating still count toward the cap, and entries sharing local data are refused

records.title: A live run's lock on the same host was taken over once 12 hours old, though a first backfill at the API budget can take longer and a Mac that sleeps mid-run looks old.
records.description: A live run's lock on the same host was taken over once 12 hours old, though a first backfill at the API budget can take longer and a Mac that sleeps mid-run looks old. On this host a lock is now stale only when its pid is gone; from another host, when it has not been touched for 12 hours, and a run touches its lock after each artifact.

test.name: R-ARC-12: a live run on this host keeps its lock however long it runs; one on another host keeps it while it touches it

records.title: Two runs judging one lock stale at once could both take it over, the second removing the lock the first had just taken.
records.description: Two runs judging one lock stale at once could both take it over, the second removing the lock the first had just taken. A takeover now runs under its own `mkdir` guard, `.lock.takeover`, and only if the owner file still names the holder judged stale.

test.name: R-ARC-13: two runs cannot both take over one stale lock, nor take one another run has just taken

records.title: On a case-insensitive, normalising disk (APFS), `A.tar.age` and `a.tar.age`, or NFC and NFD forms of one name, are one file; `x/./y` and `a//b` pass the zip reader.
records.description: On a case-insensitive, normalising disk (APFS), `A.tar.age` and `a.tar.age`, or NFC and NFD forms of one name, are one file; `x/./y` and `a//b` pass the zip reader. Writing them failed with EEXIST, which was retried, so the artifact looped until it expired and was lost with no quarantine copy. Names are now compared folded, empty and `.` parts and any-case `.artifact.json` are refused, and a name the disk cannot write sends the whole download to quarantine.

test.name: R-ARC-14: names that one disk folds together, and empty or "." parts, are refused; a name the disk cannot write sends the whole download to quarantine

records.title: Index and manifest appends and the cursor were not durable: a power loss could keep a cursor past lines that never reached the disk.
records.description: Index and manifest appends and the cursor were not durable: a power loss could keep a cursor past lines that never reached the disk. Appends are now fsynced, and the cursor (and `.last-ok.json`) is replaced through a synced temporary file and rename, after the lines.

test.name: R-ARC-15: index and manifest lines are synced to disk, and the cursor is replaced whole only after them

records.title: Found by: review (present since the archive pull began).
records.description: Found by: review (present since the archive pull began). An artifact is now pulled only if its run is in this repository (not a fork), on `main`, and from the workflow that makes that kind; others are logged and left, not quarantined and not a failure.

test.name: R-ARC-16: an artifact not made by our own workflow on main is refused unread, not quarantined, and not a failure

records.title: NIT.

records.title: NIT.
records.description: NIT. An artifact whose `created_at` is not a date failed once, then was silently left out of every later run by the cursor's look-back filter. It is now kept in the list, so it keeps failing visibly.

test.name: R-ARC-18: an artifact whose created_at is not a date keeps failing visibly on later runs
R-ARC-10: an ingest artifact whose created_at is not a date fails with that message

records.title: The state asset is overwritten on every pump run and had no versioned copy (DESIGN-v3 §2, F6, promised one): a damaged or deleted asset would restart the loop from empty.
records.description: The state asset is overwritten on every pump run and had no versioned copy (DESIGN-v3 §2, F6, promised one): a damaged or deleted asset would restart the loop from empty. Hourly snapshots now keep the 48 newest copies and the newest of each UTC day for 30 days, counted in snapshots, not hours, so an idle loop never ages out what it relies on. Retention is now 24 newest, 14 daily and 8 weekly (loop upgrade #14).

test.name: R-SNAP-01: retention keeps the 24 newest, the newest of each UTC day for 14 days and of each UTC week for 8 weeks, and prunes the rest
R-SNAP-01: an idle loop prunes nothing: retention counts snapshots, not hours

records.title: Without dedupe an idle loop would fill the 48 hourly places with identical copies and push older, different states out.
records.description: Without dedupe an idle loop would fill the 48 hourly places with identical copies and push older, different states out. A run whose live sha256 equals the newest snapshot uploads nothing and only refreshes `current_at`; a return to an older state is a new snapshot.

test.name: R-SNAP-02: dedupe compares against the newest snapshot only
R-SNAP-02: an unchanged state uploads nothing but refreshes current_at
R-SNAP-02: a changed state is a new snapshot, and so is a return to an older state

records.title: A snapshot that does not read back intact is worse than none, since it is only found out during a restore.
records.description: A snapshot that does not read back intact is worse than none, since it is only found out during a restore. Each snapshot is checked against its manifest entry (sha256, size, name, age ciphertext); a new upload is downloaded back and checked before the manifest names it, and deleted if it fails.

test.name: R-SNAP-03: verifySnapshot accepts the bytes the manifest describes and refuses a changed byte, a wrong size, a wrong name or plaintext
R-SNAP-03: an upload that does not read back intact is deleted and the run fails

records.title: The snapshot runs outside the pump's concurrency group, so the pump can replace the asset while it is being copied.
records.description: The snapshot runs outside the pump's concurrency group, so the pump can replace the asset while it is being copied. The copy must match the asset's sha256 label and the asset must be unchanged (id, label, `updated_at`) after the download, else it is copied once more, then the run fails. An unlabelled or plaintext asset is never copied.

test.name: R-SNAP-04: the pump pushing during the copy is detected and the copy is retried once
R-SNAP-04: bytes that do not match the label, twice, fail the run and upload nothing
R-SNAP-04: an interrupted pump push (temporary name only) is copied like the pump would read it
R-SNAP-04: a plaintext or unlabelled state asset is never copied

records.title: A lost manifest or a failed delete must not lose or strand snapshots.
records.description: A lost manifest or a failed delete must not lose or strand snapshots. The manifest is reconciled with the assets on every run (missing entries rebuilt from name and label, stale entries dropped) and is written before any pruned asset is deleted.

test.name: R-SNAP-05: a lost manifest is rebuilt from the snapshot assets, and a stale entry is dropped
R-SNAP-05: pruned snapshots are deleted only after the manifest that drops them is written

records.title: The snapshot job copies a public ciphertext and must hold nothing more: only `contents: write`, no environment, no secrets, no age identity, never decrypts, and the kill switch first.
records.description: The snapshot job copies a public ciphertext and must hold nothing more: only `contents: write`, no environment, no secrets, no age identity, never decrypts, and the kill switch first.

test.name: R-SNAP-06: the snapshot workflow holds only contents: write, no secrets or key, and checks the kill switch first

records.title: There was no tested way to put a snapshot back.
records.description: There was no tested way to put a snapshot back. The drill verifies a snapshot against the manifest before decrypting it, decrypts locally without printing the key, runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` and reports the counts, and leaves no plaintext. `--apply` runs only while the loop is stopped and no pump or ingest run is active, snapshots the live state first, keeps the replaced asset renamed, and changes nothing if the live asset moves during the restore.

test.name: R-SNAP-07: inspectDatabase reports integrity, schema version, the fence and row counts, subjects and results first
R-SNAP-07: the drill verifies, decrypts and checks a snapshot with the age identity, and leaves no plaintext behind
R-SNAP-07: a snapshot whose bytes differ from the manifest is refused before it is decrypted
R-SNAP-07: a snapshot that decrypts to a damaged database fails the drill
R-SNAP-07: --apply needs the loop stopped: switched off, pump lane off, or paused for at least 10 more minutes
R-SNAP-07: --apply refuses while the loop runs or a pump run is active, and changes nothing
R-SNAP-07: --apply keeps the live state as a snapshot first, then puts the chosen snapshot back byte for byte
R-SNAP-07: --apply replaces a live asset that cannot be copied, and keeps it renamed
R-SNAP-07: --apply leaves the live state alone if it changes during the restore
R-SNAP-07: a snapshot that opens but fails PRAGMA integrity_check fails the drill with report.ok false

records.title: Snapshots that silently stop are found out only when one is needed.
records.description: Snapshots that silently stop are found out only when one is needed. The health item is amber when no run has confirmed the live state is captured for 3 hours (or there is no snapshot yet) and red after 6, measured from `current_at` so an idle loop stays green.

R-SNAP-08: age is measured from current_at, so an idle loop with running snapshots stays green
R-SNAP-08: no snapshot yet or an unreadable manifest is amber; a lane switched off is off

records.description: Nothing watched the snapshots: if the hourly run stopped (the GitHub schedule on this repository has not fired reliably), nobody would know until a restore was needed. records.title: A snapshot asset the manifest did not list was adopted on the word of its label, without a download: a failed read-back whose delete also failed (or a read-back that threw) left an orphan that became…
records.description: A snapshot asset the manifest did not list was adopted on the word of its label, without a download: a failed read-back whose delete also failed (or a read-back that threw) left an orphan that became the newest snapshot, so dedupe said unchanged, health said green, and the drill failed. Unlisted assets are now downloaded and verified first (deleted if they fail, left alone if unreadable), dedupe uses verified entries only, any read-back failure deletes the upload, and the drill checks an unlisted snapshot against its label.

test.name: R-SNAP-10: an asset the manifest does not list is verified before it is adopted; one that fails is deleted and never used for dedupe
R-SNAP-10: an unlisted asset that cannot be downloaded is left alone and not trusted
R-SNAP-10: a read-back that throws deletes the upload and fails the run
R-SNAP-10: the drill can use a snapshot the manifest does not list, checked against its own label

records.title: `restore --apply` kept only an asset named exactly `state.sqlite` and deleted every `state.sqlite.upload-*`.
records.description: `restore --apply` kept only an asset named exactly `state.sqlite` and deleted every `state.sqlite.upload-*`. After an interrupted pump push the live state is such an upload; with the pre-restore snapshot also failing, the live state would have been lost. The live asset itself, whatever its name, is now renamed to `state.sqlite.replaced-*`; only other stale uploads are deleted.

records.description: `parseManifest` accepted any array: a null entry crashed every run, and an entry's `created` came from the manifest, so a future date pinned it as newest for good and broke dedupe. Every entry is now checked (snapshot name, a 64-hex sha256 the name carries), `created` always comes from the name, and snapshots dated in the future are left out.

R-SNAP-13: the loop switches are read as the pump job sees them: environment, then repository, then every organization page

records.description: Losing the copy race with the pump on both tries failed the run (red on the health issue) although nothing was wrong. It now never throws (amber instead), treats a time more than 5 minutes ahead as amber, and tells no release, no manifest and an empty manifest apart.

records.title: MEDIUM-LOW.
records.description: MEDIUM-LOW. A snapshot manifest with two or more null entries made the newest-snapshot sort throw, and `evaluate()` is not in a try, so the whole watchdog run failed and the health issue was not written. The parser now drops such entries (R-SNAP-12), `snapshotCheck` never throws (R-SNAP-16), and the watchdog fences it anyway: anything unexpected is an amber item. A missing release, a missing manifest and a time in the future are amber with their own wording.

records.title: A lock on this host whose pid had been reused (after a reboot the pid can belong to anything, even pid 1) was never taken over, so the archive stopped until someone removed it.
records.description: A lock on this host whose pid had been reused (after a reboot the pid can belong to anything, even pid 1) was never taken over, so the archive stopped until someone removed it. `owner.json` now records the host's boot time, and a lock from an earlier boot, or whose pid `ps` shows running something other than `archive-pull`, is stale. OPERATIONS says how to remove the lock by hand. Refined by R-ARC-23 and R-ARC-24: the pid's command line now decides first, and the boot time only when `ps` cannot tell.

test.name: R-ARC-19: a lock on this host from an earlier boot, or whose pid now runs another program, is taken over

records.title: Our own artifacts were refused silently when a workflow was renamed or added: one from this repository on `main` but from a workflow `SOURCES` did not list got a log line only, and the cursor moved p…
records.description: Our own artifacts were refused silently when a workflow was renamed or added: one from this repository on `main` but from a workflow `SOURCES` did not list got a log line only, and the cursor moved past it, so it was never archived. It is now held: a failure (exit 1, a notification, the cursor stays) until `SOURCES` lists the workflow; refusals of forks and other branches stay silent. A test maps every `upload-artifact` name prefix in `.github/workflows/` to `SOURCES`.

test.name: R-ARC-20: our own artifact from a workflow SOURCES does not list is held, retried and notified, not passed over
R-ARC-20: every artifact a workflow here uploads under an archived prefix is mapped in SOURCES to that workflow

test.name: R-ARC-21: many runs are looked up from the run list a page at a time, with one GET for each run it does not find

records.title: Nothing on GitHub watched the archive heartbeat `ARCHIVE_LAST_OK`, so an archive that stopped was seen only on the Mac.
records.description: Nothing on GitHub watched the archive heartbeat `ARCHIVE_LAST_OK`, so an archive that stopped was seen only on the Mac. The watchdog now has an `archive` item, read from `${{ vars.ARCHIVE_LAST_OK }}` through `env:` (the job token cannot read variables through the API): amber after 12 hours or dated in the future, red after 24 hours or when empty, not JSON, or without a valid `at`.

test.name: R-ARC-22: the watchdog shows the archive heartbeat from vars.ARCHIVE_LAST_OK: amber after 12 hours, red after 24 or when it is empty or unreadable
R-ARC-22: watchdog.yml passes vars.ARCHIVE_LAST_OK to the watchdog step through env

records.title: macOS moves `kern.boottime` when the clock is set, so a wall-clock jump of more than 2 minutes made a live pull's lock look like one from an earlier boot, and a second run could take it over.
records.description: macOS moves `kern.boottime` when the clock is set, so a wall-clock jump of more than 2 minutes made a live pull's lock look like one from an earlier boot, and a second run could take it over. A live pid that is not ours and whose `ps` line contains `archive-pull.mjs` (or is the holder's recorded line, R-ARC-24) is now live whatever the boot time; the boot time decides only when `ps` cannot tell. The match is on `archive-pull.mjs`, not `archive-pull`, which a `tail -f` of the log also matched; `ps` runs with `-ww` so a line is never cut; a lock naming our own pid is stale.

test.name: R-ARC-23: a live archive pull keeps its lock across a clock jump; the boot time is used only when ps cannot tell

records.title: A pull started through a wrapper or a link without `archive-pull` in its command line had its live lock taken over.
records.description: A pull started through a wrapper or a link without `archive-pull` in its command line had its live lock taken over. `owner.json` now records the holder's own `ps` command line, and a pid still showing that line keeps the lock.

test.name: R-ARC-24: a run started through a wrapper or link records its own command line, and keeps its lock by it

records.title: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10).
records.description: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10). A release tag force-pushed to another commit was invisible: nothing recorded what each tag pointed to. meta-github now reads the newest 100 tags with their targets in its existing GraphQL batch (`git_tag_targets`, `git_tag_map_sha256`), and `longitudinal/derive.mjs` reports a version-like tag whose commit changed between two observations as a `git_tag_moves` event, ranked high.

test.name: R-DRIFT-01: a version-like release tag force-pushed to another commit is a git_tag_moves event, ranked high
R-DRIFT-01: meta-github records each tag's target (an annotated tag peeled once) and a hash of the tag map, in the same GraphQL batch

records.title: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10).
records.description: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10). An image tag that moved to a new image was invisible: the loop never recorded which digest a declared OCI tag resolved to. meta-registry now resolves up to five declared tags per subject with a manifest HEAD (`oci_tag_digests`), and a version-like tag with a new digest is an `oci_tag_moves` event, ranked medium (R-DRIFT-19).

test.name: R-DRIFT-02: a version-like image tag that resolves to a new digest is an oci_tag_moves event, ranked medium; latest moving is not
R-DRIFT-02: an image tag resolves to its digest with a manifest HEAD, one anonymous token per image, never a GET on docker.io

records.title: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10).
records.description: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10). A tool list that changed without a release had no signal. A changed tool list hash behind the same image digest is a `catalog_drift_same_version` event (`catalog_changed_same_image`, medium); behind a version tag that now points to a new digest, `catalog_changed_with_tag_move` (high).

test.name: R-DRIFT-03: a tool list that changes behind an unchanged image digest is a catalog_drift_same_version event; a new digest behind the same tag ranks high

records.title: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10), false-positive guard.
records.description: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10), false-positive guard. Floating tags (`latest`, `main`, `v1`, `1.2`) are meant to move. Only a full MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag, optionally v- or package-prefixed, can be an event; floating moves are counted, and a version tag re-annotated on the same commit is not a move.

test.name: R-DRIFT-04: version-like means a full MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, optionally v- or package-prefixed; floating tags are not
R-DRIFT-04: floating tags (latest, v1, v1.4, nightly, main) moving are counted, never events; a re-annotated version tag on the same commit is not a move

records.title: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10), false-positive guard.
records.description: Found by: loop tooling upgrades (item 10), false-positive guard. Re-tagging minutes after a release is a common fix-up. A git tag whose old and new targets were made within an hour of each other, or an image tag whose old digest was last seen within an hour of the release, is kept but ranked low. records.description: Found by: the merge gate on the first ledger pull request (18). The pull request was opened with the job token, which starts no pull_request workflows, so it had no checks at all. After each new refresh commit the publish job now sets the commit statuses dispatched/test and dispatched/lint to pending and dispatches test.yml and lint.yml on ledger/refresh (workflow_dispatch is the one event the job token may start). A dispatched run's check runs do not show on a pull request (probe pull request 22: both runs passed on its head, `gh pr checks` reported no checks), so each workflow's report job sets its commit status to the run's result, and commit statuses do show. records.description: Found by: the 27 Nov log review (nine subjects `too_large`: large Python, C#, Rust and monorepo packages). records.description: Found by: 26 Nov, two live-probe runs failed at `sandbox / sandbox-selftest` (mcp-check runs 45745127857 and 45747519135; a runsc logging race, since fixed, and a control mismatch). The guard fails closed, so nothing ran and the items came back `no_artifact`, but the health issue read green: `sandbox-breaker` reads only the nightly status, so a runner image rollout that broke the self test on the lanes' runners would have stopped the lanes unseen. New item `sandbox-selftest` (`watchdog/selftest.mjs`): reads the failed runs of the last 7 hours of each enabled lane that runs third-party code (live-probe, writecheck), counts self-test job failures in the last 6 hours and reads the runner image of the newest 3 from the job log header. The job `GITHUB_TOKEN` gets 403 on other repositories' job logs, so the image was always unknown (found in review of #91): a second App token, `actions: read` for the lane repositories, reads them, with a fallback to the job token (amber with the reason). Amber on 2 or more in 6 hours, or one on an image the nightly has not passed on (an unreadable image counts), or a failed lookup; never red; green otherwise; off with no such lane.

records.title: Found by: the 25 Nov 2026 GitHub outage (15:55 to 16:36 UTC).
records.description: Found by: the 25 Nov 2026 GitHub outage (15:55 to 16:36 UTC). Every GitHub call in the loop had its own retry or none: the pump's REST client tried 4 times in about 7 seconds, the state asset client never repeated a POST, the snapshot client repeated nothing it posted. One burst of HTTP 500 on the successor dispatch broke the pump chain. One policy now (`pump/retry.mjs`): HTTP 500, 502, 503, 504, 429, a 403 with a rate-limit signal and network errors or timeouts are retried; any other 4xx is not. Up to 6 attempts, exponential delay with full jitter (2 s base, 120 s cap), `Retry-After` honoured up to 60 s (a longer one ends the retries), bounded by a total-sleep cap and an absolute deadline; each retry is logged (call, attempt n/6, reason, delay) with no token.

test.name: R-CHAOS-13: only 500, 502, 503, 504, 429, network errors and rate-limited 403s are transient; other 4xx are final
R-CHAOS-13: the delay is exponential with full jitter: base 2 s, doubling, cap 120 s
R-CHAOS-13: Retry-After is honoured and capped at 60 s; a longer one ends the retries
R-CHAOS-13: the retrier stops at the attempt limit, the total-sleep limit and the deadline, and logs each retry

records.title: Found by: the 25 Nov 2026 outage (HTTP 500 and 502 on the state asset upload).
records.description: Found by: the 25 Nov 2026 outage (HTTP 500 and 502 on the state asset upload). A state push stopped at the first server error, and a plain repeat of an upload that GitHub had stored would have failed as `already_exists` or left two copies. The state asset and snapshot clients now repeat an upload only after reading the release: a complete asset of that name with the same size and label is the upload and is used as it is, a partial or different one is deleted first. The unchanged-remote checks of the push (fencing) still run on the result, so a retried push cannot overwrite newer state. A release create is looked up before it is repeated.

test.name: R-CHAOS-14: a push whose upload gets HTTP 500 and 502 is repeated until it lands, with backoff, and logs the retries
R-CHAOS-14: an upload that was stored but answered 500 is not uploaded twice: the stored copy is used, and the push still checks the remote is unchanged
R-CHAOS-14: a half-stored upload under the same name is deleted before the repeat, and a rival asset that appeared still refuses the push
R-CHAOS-14: pull retries a server error on the release read and on the asset download
R-CHAOS-14: a short GitHub outage on the state push (500s on the upload, then a 502) is ridden out by the retries: the run does not fail and nothing is saved twice

It now tries 6 times (token mint and dispatch together inside a 90 second window, so the job's time is safe) and still fails closed: after the last try it records the failure, marks `pump-successor` red and the pump goes on. records.title: Found by: design of R-CHAOS-13.
records.description: Found by: design of R-CHAOS-13. What is not retried is part of the contract: any other 4xx (a refusal does not pass), and a POST that may already have been carried out, which the pump's shard dispatch is (a repeat could start a second run for one lease and attempt). Only a call marked harmless to repeat (the successor and registry dispatches, token mints) or one with a recovery step (uploads) is repeated after a 5xx or a network error.

records.title: Found by: design of R-CHAOS-13.
records.description: Found by: design of R-CHAOS-13. Retries must not make a run overrun its job's timeout-minutes or hold on past the run's deadline. A push takes a `retryUntil` (a tick's push: the run's deadline; the last push: 90 seconds past it) and a total-sleep cap (180 s; the snapshot client 300 s); when the next delay would pass either, the call stops and the error is marked transient. `pump.yml` timeout-minutes is 20 (was 15) for the successor's 90 s and the last push's grace.

records.title: Found by: design (loop project item "Lane version pins are labels only: workers run ref main").
records.description: Found by: design (loop project item "Lane version pins are labels only: workers run ref main"). A lane's `versions.tool` and `versions.probe` go into every run_key, but the pump dispatched each worker on its branch (`ref: main`), so a result filed under a pin could have run whatever was on the worker's main: the label could lie. The pump now sends a lane's own pinned commit as `tool_sha` on a `pin_check: enforce` lane (a pin it cannot resolve is not dispatched), and ingest checks every bundle's manifest `tools` against the run_key's pins: another version is refused as `pin_mismatch` on every lane, an unproven one as `pin_unverified` on an enforce lane (accepted with a note on a `label` lane, the rollout setting). Tool fault side, not counted towards parking, lane paused for an hour. Mutation-checked: 13 protections turned off one at a time, each caught.

records.title: Found by: design audit 27 Nov (A3).

records.description: Found by: design audit (A3). A new commit on the default branch was never seen. test.name: R-CHG-02: a new head moves sha and changed_at (new_sha); the same head writes nothing

records.title: Found by: design audit (A3).
records.description: Found by: design audit (A3). A release cut on an unchanged commit was never seen. A release published after `changed_at` now moves `changed_at` (`new_release`, due as `change_event`), once; a release dated ahead of our clock is not believed.

test.name: R-CHG-03: a release published after the last change at the same head is a change_event, seen once; a release dated in the future is not believed

records.title: Found by: design (never blame a server for our limit).
records.description: Found by: design (never blame a server for our limit). test.name: R-CHG-05: the budget guard: at most MAX_QUERIES a run, a budget refusal or a low point count stops the pass, and the cursor moves only past applied answers

records.title: Found by: design (DESIGN-v3 4.3 cadences).
records.description: Found by: design (DESIGN-v3 4.3 cadences). Polling everyone every run would waste the budget, and a cursor left past retired subjects would stick a tier for good. Tiers are walked in cycles from a kv cursor (`head_poll_hours`: T0 every run, T1 hourly, T3 daily), one query mixes tiers, and a cursor with nothing left closes its cycle.

test.name: R-CHG-06: cadence by tier: T0 every run, T3 once a day, a cycle resumes from its cursor and one query mixes tiers

records.title: Found by: review of #98.
records.description: Found by: review of #98. One bad node wedged the poll for good: any GraphQL error but NOT_FOUND made the whole batch an error, so the cursor never moved (one FORBIDDEN node, 3 runs, 0 written). An error under `nodes[i]` now marks entry i only; one only under `nodes[i].latestRelease` loses the release and keeps the head; an error with no node path still fails the query, which is asked again.

test.name: R-CHG-09: one bad node never wedges the poll: a FORBIDDEN node is an error for that entry only, an error under latestRelease loses only the release, an error with no node path fails the batch

records.title: Found by: review of #98.
records.description: Found by: review of #98. A subject in id conflict keeps its `repo_id`/`node_id`, so the head of repository A could have landed on a subject whose name clones repository B. Only `id_status = ok` subjects are polled, and a node whose `nameWithOwner` is not `subjects.name` (renamed since the id pass) is skipped as `renamed`.

test.name: R-CHG-10: only subjects the id pass vouches for (id_status ok) are polled, and a node renamed since then is skipped as renamed

records.title: Found by: review of #98.
records.description: Found by: review of #98. The 200-point reserve was checked only after a query, the id pass could be squeezed out of the shared hourly `graphql` calls, and a large T0 could take every pick. Before the first query the pass makes none under 200 known points and leaves the last 8 hourly calls to the id pass; T0 takes at most a quarter of a run. The point count is carried across runs with the budget (`ApiBudget.restore` now restores `resources` until their reset).

test.name: R-CHG-11: the budget is checked before the first query (points reserve, calls held for the id pass), and T0 takes at most a quarter of a run

records.title: Found by: the live loop (28 Nov, from 00:52Z).
records.description: Found by: the live loop (28 Nov, from 00:52Z). #113 moved live-probe's `mcp-check` pin to dbfea01 and left `versions.probe.fuzz` at bece344. The worker reports the fuzz stage at its own commit, so every live-probe result was refused as `pin_mismatch` (fuzz: pinned bece344, reported dbfea01…) and the lane paused hour after hour. Nothing checked that the shipped pins were ones the worker could prove. The test now builds what the worker reports from the shipped pins and needs it accepted, holds the fuzz pin to the mcp-check pin and every probe `mcp-surface-corpus` pin to its lane's `sandbox_sha`, and keeps a stale pin a tool-side refusal.

records.title: Found by: loop design audit (writecheck min and full modes, 27 Nov).
records.description: Found by: loop design audit (writecheck min and full modes, 27 Nov). Workers squeezed new cases into generic reasons (`unsupported_layout`, `policy_excluded`, `heavy_backend`, `no_runnable_artifact`) and kept the real cause in `logs/driver.json`, where coverage cannot see it. A skip may now carry a bounded `code` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,47}$`; a bad one makes the manifest invalid, our worker's fault), ingest keeps it in the state (`results.skip_codes`, schema 13), and six reasons exist for stand-ins: `mock_incomplete`, `stand_in_mismatch`, `declaration_missing`, `backend_semantics_not_exercised` (tool), `target_not_standin` and `not_testable_backend` (policy by default, tool allowed). None may say `subject`. `start_requires_credentials` may say `tool` only with a `start_against_*` code (the start ran against our own mock or stand-in); its default stays `subject`.

test.name: R-COV-49: walking SKIP_REASONS, the six stand-in reasons allow tool and never subject
R-COV-49: a skip code is optional, bounded to the pattern, and a bad one makes the manifest invalid
R-COV-49: start_requires_credentials may say tool only when its code says the start ran against our own mock or stand-in
R-COV-49: skipCodes lists each distinct (fault, code) pair of a bundle, skips without a usable code add nothing
R-COV-49: a skip code is carried to the ledger with its fault; a code outside the pattern refuses the bundle
R-COV-49: recordResult keeps the skip codes of an accepted result as JSON, and NULL when there are none

records.title: Found by: coverage review of 26 Nov (`unsupported_package`: 43 MCP bundle subjects of 97) and design.
records.description: Found by: coverage review of 26 Nov (`unsupported_package`: 43 MCP bundle subjects of 97) and design. A bundle could not run at all, and reading one is reading an archive from a release page. The planner reads it as data (corpus/mcpb.mjs): from its GitHub release asset only, every redirect checked, at most 200 MiB, the registry's fileSha256 checked, every entry name checked as the sandbox checks it, manifest.json at most 1 MiB, the first bytes of a binary; and builds the launch a client would (server.type, mcp_config with the linux override and the client's variables; a required user_config value with no default is `start_needs_config`, never guessed; an optional one is left out with its flag; names the sandbox owns are never set; PYTHONPATH stays inside the bundle; a binary only when linux is listed and it is a linux/amd64 ELF; a shell launcher is not started; `uv run` read as uv reads it). The sandbox unpacks only the bytes with the pinned sha256 (mcp-surface-corpus R-SBX-36, R-SBX-41, R-SBX-42). The bundle's own fault only for its own evidence (`bundle_unavailable`, `bundle_hash_mismatch`, `bundle_invalid`, `package_not_runnable`); and only for an entry in the subject's namespace (security review of #53: anyone can publish an entry naming someone else's repository with a dead bundle URL; a repository-only entry gives `unverified_registry_entry`, a seed-only or seed-matched one `bundle_unowned`, new, tool; the 404 is asked twice); a bare launcher (npx, sh, bun, docker ...) is `bundle_runtime_unsupported`, never the bundle's; only a name that leaves the bundle is `bundle_invalid`, others `bundle_unreadable`; a path the manifest names is the bundle's missing file (`package_not_runnable`) only when it names nothing the bundle holds, not one its runtime resolves (node's `.js`, a folder, a Windows `.exe`) nor one in another case (`platform_unsupported`), and `uv run <command>` with no pyproject is a launcher (re-check of #53, 27 Nov); a node or python script outside the bundle (an absolute path of the author's machine, one that climbs out, a relative one the bundle does not hold) is `bundle_runtime_unsupported`, never started to crash as the bundle's (review of 27 Nov); so is a file a node option loads first (`-r`, `--require`, `--import`, `--loader`, `--experimental-loader`, `--env-file`, either form) outside the bundle or not held (a package name such as `dotenv/config` stays allowed, an env file the bundle does not ship is ours), and the command line is read as the runtime reads it: node's value options (`--disable-warning X`) and python's grouped flags and attached values (`-uW ignore`, `-Wmodule`, `--check-hash-based-pycs X`) never hide the script or pass for it (second review of #53); a run of slashes (`${__dirname}/lib//a.mjs`) names the file it would without them, never a missing one, and a module from the home folder (`~/h.js`), any scheme but `node:` and `data:` (`https:`, `jsr:` ...), or a `file:` URL with a host or an encoded `/` or `\` is ours (third review of #53); our limits first when one subject's bundles fail for both. Mutation check per guard.

Review follow-up: a bare registrar on a non-MCP object (pydantic-ai `agent.tool`, `tracer.tool`) made tools; `tool` imported from fastmcp went through the repository's own factory; line numbers were counted quadratically.

test.name: R-RD-02: a registrar used as a bare decorator (@create_tool("x", "X") calling add_tool): each decorated function is a tool, named after the function
R-RD-02: a bare registrar that passes one of its parameters on as the name: the name comes from that argument
R-RD-02: a decorator factory that builds the tool dict from its parameters: name, title and description from the arguments
R-RD-02: a helper that returns the tool dict: each call is a tool, the schema filled from the arguments
R-RD-02: a factory call whose name the reader cannot work out is counted as unresolved, never invented
R-RD-02: a function of the same name defined twice in the repository is not used as a factory
R-RD-02: a bare registrar on something that is not an MCP server (pydantic-ai agent.tool, tracer.tool) makes no tool
R-RD-02: @tool imported from fastmcp is the SDK's decorator, even when the repository has its own tool() factory
R-RD-02: many factory calls in one long logical line are read in linear time

records.title: Found by: loop assessment (L19).
records.description: Found by: loop assessment (L19). scan-static recorded every lasting skip as `no_runnable_artifact`, so our own limits (no tools found, an unsupported language or layout, names only, a reader limit, a list too large, a reader or bundle error) read as the subject's in tool-qa and could be counted as excluded. Each detail code now has its own tool-qa reason and a fault side (`tool`, `subject`, `infra`); only a repository that is gone, private, blocked or empty is the subject's. Worker kit pinned at tool-qa 2ffcea1, which accepts them.

test.name: R-SS-14: every detail code is recorded with a tool-qa reason and a fault its reason allows; our own limits are never the subject's
R-SS-14: a reader limit reaches tool-qa as our own: valid under the pinned contract, unassessed_tool, never excluded or the subject's
R-SS-14: a list too large to hold (list_rejected / too_large) is recorded as too_large

records.title: Nothing measured how often mcp-check is fooled, and nothing stopped a release when a check started missing what it used to find: no ground-truth cases, no precision or recall per check and language (…
records.description: Nothing measured how often mcp-check is fooled, and nothing stopped a release when a check started missing what it used to find: no ground-truth cases, no precision or recall per check and language (design §10.2). Now `bench/` scores every case against its truth, and the required `bench` job of `ci.yml` fails when a check's false negatives rise or its recall falls below the baseline interval.

test.name: R-BENCH-01: the gate fails when a check's false negatives rise, or its recall drops below the baseline interval

records.title: A scorer that only echoed its labels would have looked perfect: nothing proved it reads mcp-check's output.
records.description: A scorer that only echoed its labels would have looked perfect: nothing proved it reads mcp-check's output. Faulty-oracle cases (labels wrong on purpose) must each come out as a disagreement, or the run and the gate fail.

test.name: R-BENCH-02: a faulty-oracle label is reported as a disagreement, never echoed as a pass

records.title: The ~200 mcp-check mutants of design §4.6 did not exist, so nothing showed that the cases would catch a broken reader or check.
records.description: The ~200 mcp-check mutants of design §4.6 did not exist, so nothing showed that the cases would catch a broken reader or check. `bench/mutate.mjs` runs about 170 source and 42 fixture mutants weekly and on reader or check changes (`bench-mutants.yml`), and fails when a mutant on the kill list survives.

test.name: R-BENCH-03: the mutant pass catches a planted check bug, and fails when a mutant on the kill list survives

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. Four core checks (`sec-invisible-encoding`, `sec-homoglyph`, `sec-control-chars`, `spec-name-length`) had no positive case and four security checks had one, so a build with any of them switched off passed the gate. Every security check now has at least 3 hand-labelled positives in 2 or more languages, and every other core check at least 1.

test.name: R-BENCH-04: every core check has labelled positives: at least 3 in 2 languages for each security check, at least 1 for the others

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. The gate only warned on false-positive rises: a bug raising `spec-name-charset` on 111 tools passed, and 11 of 50 ground-truth-killed mutants passed the required gate. Rises now fail for `sec-*`, `reader-tools` and `security-cap`, and past the precision interval for the rest, and the mutant pass kills by the gate's own compare().

test.name: R-BENCH-05: false-positive rises fail the gate (any for security, reader-tools and the cap; past the interval for the rest), and a planted false-alarm bug is a gate kill

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. The gate compared totals, so one case getting worse was cancelled by another getting better. The baseline now stores each case's disagreement keys, and any new one fails.

test.name: R-BENCH-06: one case getting worse fails the gate even when another case gets better

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. Coverage could be dropped silently (fewer cases, removed labels, edited truth), and gains were never locked in. The gate now fails when true positives or the case count fall, when the case-set hash is not the baseline's, and when the score beats the baseline (rebaseline with `node bench/run.mjs --rebaseline`).

test.name: R-BENCH-07: lost coverage, a changed case set and unlocked improvements fail the gate

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. SCORE.md showed 31 checks as measured although all their positives came from labels drafted from the engine's output. They are now listed apart as "inferred labels, self-consistency only".

test.name: R-BENCH-08: checks whose positives all come from inferred labels are reported apart, as self-consistency only

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. A faulty-oracle case counted as caught on any disagreement. Each now names the one disagreement its wrong label must cause, and only that one counts.

test.name: R-BENCH-09: a faulty-oracle case is caught only by the disagreement its truth names

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. The holdout guard relied on the `split` field alone. `bench/holdout-hashes.json` (hashes only) now lets the suite refuse any public case or truth file that matches a holdout file, also with its whitespace changed.

test.name: R-BENCH-10: no public case or truth file matches a holdout file hash

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. The mutant pass was not required by `ci-ok`, the gate step was not pinned by a test, and Dependabot could pick up the cases' package.json files. The pass is now the `mutants` job of `ci.yml`, required by `ci-ok`; the steps are pinned; `bench/**` is excluded from Dependabot.

test.name: R-BENCH-11: the bench gate and the mutant pass are required by ci-ok, and their steps are pinned

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. The header of `bench/mutate.mjs` said `--sample` was the pull-request run; CI runs the full set.

test.name: R-BENCH-12: --sample runs a fixed subset of the full mutant set, as the header says

records.title: Found by: review of #31.
records.description: Found by: review of #31. Saved lists went to the system temp folder, so a mutant child killed at its time limit left `bench-save-*` folders behind. They now go in the run's own folder, inside the mutant pass's folder.

test.name: R-BENCH-13: the saved lists go in the run's own folder, which is removed, and nothing is left in the system temp folder

records.title: Found by: re-review of #31.
records.description: Found by: re-review of #31. The gate compared only with the baseline in the same pull request, so a pull request could switch a check off, rebaseline (or shrink the kill list with --write-expected) and pass. The bench job now also compares with the base branch's baseline and kill list, and fails on anything worse unless the pull request has the `bench-rebaseline` label.

test.name: R-BENCH-14: a pull request cannot accept its own regressions: new misses, false alarms and kill-list removals against the base baseline fail without the bench-rebaseline label

records.title: Found by: re-review of #31.
records.description: Found by: re-review of #31. Only mutants picked by the quota ran, so a kill-list mutant that was not picked could survive unnoticed. Every id on the kill list now runs in every pass.

test.name: R-BENCH-15: every mutant on the kill list runs in every pass, so the list only ratchets

records.title: Found by: re-review of #31.
records.description: Found by: re-review of #31. bench/holdout-hashes.json named the private holdout's path, and whitespace-free hashes of tiny boilerplate files could refuse an unrelated public file. The text now says only "the private holdout", and files under 200 bytes get only their byte hash.

test.name: R-BENCH-16: the holdout hash list names no private path, and tiny files get only their byte hash

records.title: Found by: final review of #31.
records.description: Found by: final review of #31. The base-branch guard could be bypassed through the truth files: a mutant's false alarm on `render_chart` written into `truth/typescript/computed-parts.json` as a label, then rebaselined, gave 0 findings and needed no label. Every case or truth file of the base that a pull request changes or deletes is now a finding.

test.name: R-BENCH-17: a label edited to match a new false alarm is caught: every case or truth file of the base that is changed or deleted is a finding

records.title: Found by: final review of #31.
records.description: Found by: final review of #31. Only gate.mjs and base-guard.mjs were watched, and through the guard's own code, so a pull request editing the scorer, the mutant pass, their tests or ci.yml, or the guard itself, passed. The bench job's step now checks a fixed list of those paths itself and fails without the `bench-rebaseline` label.

test.name: R-BENCH-18: changes to the benchmark's machinery need the bench-rebaseline label, checked in the workflow itself, not by the guard

records.title: Found by: bench (`python/docstring-unicode-escape`, `python/poison-escapes`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`python/docstring-unicode-escape`, `python/poison-escapes`). Python strings read `\uXXXX` as the letters `uXXXX` and did not decode `\xHH`, `\UXXXXXXXX` or octal (docstrings, `description=` and `name=` alike), so bidi, zero-width, tag and ANSI characters written as escapes never reached the poisoning checks, and `lookup_\u0430ccount` came out as `lookup_u0430ccount` (homoglyph missed, phantom name). Escapes are now decoded as Python decodes them; an unknown escape keeps its backslash; raw strings stay raw. Review follow-up: in a raw f-string a backslash no longer hides a `{expression}`.

test.name: R-RD-07: Python string escapes are decoded as Python decodes them (\x, \u, \U, octal); an unknown escape keeps its backslash
R-RD-07: a docstring written with \u escapes keeps the bidi characters they stand for, and the security check sees them
R-RD-07: a name= keyword is decoded, so a look-alike letter written as an escape is the name the server lists
R-RD-07: in a raw f-string a backslash stays and does not hide a {expression}

records.title: Found by: bench (`typescript/duplicate-and-bad-names`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`typescript/duplicate-and-bad-names`). A literal tools array that repeats a name was de-duplicated when read, so `spec-name-unique` and `openai-name-unique` could not fire. Both entries of one literal array are kept; a name registered twice anywhere else is still one tool. Review follow-up: a duplicate is kept only when the name's first tool came from the same file (a list in another file than the first registration made a false `spec-name-unique`).

test.name: R-RD-08: a literal tools array that repeats a name keeps both entries, so spec-name-unique can fire
R-RD-08: the same name registered twice outside one literal array is still one tool (alternatives, not a list)
R-RD-08: duplicates in a literal array of another file than the name's first registration are not kept

records.title: Found by: bench (`lists/malformed-entry`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`lists/malformed-entry`). A committed `{ "tools": [...] }` list with one entry missing `inputSchema` was ignored entirely (the repository read as having no tools), and only the bare-array form accepted `input_schema`. Both forms now take every named entry when at least one has a schema; the bad entry is graded (`spec-input-schema-missing`).

test.name: R-RD-09: a committed { tools: [...] } list with one entry missing inputSchema is read in full, the bad entry kept for its finding
R-RD-09: the bare-array and { tools } forms accept the same entries (input_schema in either), and named objects without any schema are not a list

records.title: Found by: bench (`rust/two-handlers`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`rust/two-handlers`). Two `ServerHandler` impls for different types in two modules of one crate folder were merged into one list instead of refused as two servers, as the README says. Each such module file with tools is now a group of its own (refused); the message says they are modules of one crate instead of offering a folder that cannot hold one alone.

test.name: R-RD-10: two modules of one crate that each implement ServerHandler are refused as two servers, not merged
R-RD-10: one ServerHandler module with its tools in another file of the crate is one server

records.title: Found by: bench (`go/conditional-env`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`go/conditional-env`). A Go tool added under `if os.Getenv(...) {` (or its `else`) was not marked conditional. It is now marked `conditional-branch` with the condition's text. Review follow-up: `if v := os.Getenv("X"); v == "1" {` (an init statement) is a guard too.

test.name: R-RD-11: a Go tool added under if os.Getenv(...) is marked conditional; one added unconditionally is not
R-RD-11: a Go tool under if with an init statement (if v := os.Getenv("X"); v == "1") is conditional

records.title: Found by: bench (`typescript/factory-function`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`typescript/factory-function`). A repository function that returns a tool object, called with an annotation argument (`keyTool('get_key', '…', true)`), was read like `server.tool(name, description)`: its literal `inputSchema` and its annotations were lost, and not marked unreadable. Such calls are now read with the function's parameters bound to the arguments; parts built from arguments the reader cannot know are marked unreadable, as are annotations whose hint is held in a variable. Review follow-up: a factory's returned object needs a schema key (`findTool(name)` returning `{ name, found }` made a phantom tool); parameters bound through an overlay, not a copy of the constants per call.

test.name: R-RD-12: a tool factory called with an annotation argument keeps its literal inputSchema and the annotations it is given
R-RD-12: an argument the reader cannot know marks that part unreadable instead of grading it as absent
R-RD-12: annotations with a hint held in a variable are marked unreadable in a plain registration too
R-RD-12: a TOOLISH function whose object has no schema key is not a tool factory (no phantom tool)

records.title: Found by: bench (`typescript/alias-server-variable`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`typescript/alias-server-variable`). `const register = s.registerTool.bind(s); register('ping_service', …)` was not read. A `registerTool`, `tool` or `addTool` bound under another name is now read like the method.

test.name: R-RD-13: registerTool bound to its server under another name is read like registerTool

records.title: Found by: bench (`lists/checks-schemas`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`lists/checks-schemas`). False positive: `annot-write-marked-readonly` fired on `resolve_names` because "resolve" was always an update. "resolve" followed by a name to look up (names, id, host, library, …) is now a read; `resolve_issue` stays an update. Engine change; `engine/VENDORED.json` records the hash. Review follow-up: `resolve_dependencies`, `resolve_imports`, `resolve_packages` and the like stay writes.

test.name: R-RD-14: resolve_names and resolve_library_id read; resolve_issue stays an update, and only the reads may be read-only
R-RD-14: resolve_dependencies and resolve_imports stay writes

records.title: Found by: bench (`typescript/loop-over-definitions`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`typescript/loop-over-definitions`). `for (const t of TOOLS) server.registerTool(t.name, …)` reported one unresolved registration even though every name in `TOOLS` was read. Registrations in a loop over a literal or constant collection read in full are now read once per element; a loop over anything else still counts as unresolved. Review follow-up: only a const of the file that nothing changes is unrolled (a `push`, a reassigned `let`, an index assignment or a call taking it keep the registration unresolved); parameters and outer loop variables hide same-named constants; an index before `.forEach` is not a literal; a body that may `continue`, `break`, `return` or `throw` first is not unrolled; constants are overlaid, not copied per element (3,000 loops beside 4,000 constants took several seconds), and the work is charged to the file's budget.

test.name: R-RD-15: a for-of loop over a table whose names are all read leaves no unresolved registration
R-RD-15: a loop over a collection the reader does not know in full still counts its registration as unresolved
R-RD-15: a collection that is changed after its declaration (push, let reassigned, index assignment) is not unrolled; its registration stays unresolved
R-RD-15: a parameter or an outer loop variable that shadows a constant is not read as the constant
R-RD-15: an index expression before .forEach is not an array literal, and a loop body that may skip the registration is not unrolled
R-RD-15: many loops and factory calls next to many constants are read in linear time

records.title: Found by: bench (`typescript/generated-template-names`) and the bug list.
records.description: Found by: bench (`typescript/generated-template-names`) and the bug list. Tool names taken from `Object.entries` (or `Object.keys`, `.forEach`, a literal array, a template) of a literal object were not read. Also: a config held in a constant lost the optional keys of its zod raw shape, so every argument read as required.

test.name: R-RD-16: tool names from Object.entries of a literal object are read, with each entry's config
R-RD-16: Object.entries(...).forEach, Object.keys, an array literal and template names are read the same way
R-RD-16: a config held in a constant keeps the optional keys of its raw shape (z.x().optional() is not required)

records.title: Found by: bench (`javascript/poison-escapes`).
records.description: Found by: bench (`javascript/poison-escapes`). JavaScript `\xHH` was read as `xHH` and `\u{XXXXX}` decoded wrongly, which missed tag characters and ANSI escapes and invented a control-character finding. Strings and templates now decode `\xHH`, `\uXXXX`, `\u{…}`, legacy octal and line continuations as the engine does.

test.name: R-RD-17: JavaScript \xHH, \u{…}, octal and line-continuation escapes are decoded as the engine decodes them

records.title: Found by: bench (surviving fixture mutant `fx-go-build-tag-default`).
records.description: Found by: bench (surviving fixture mutant `fx-go-build-tag-default`). A Go file under a build tag every default build meets (`//go:build !debugtools`, `go1.21`) had its tools marked conditional. Only constraints that some default build does not meet mark them now.

test.name: R-RD-18: a Go file under a build tag the default build meets (//go:build !debugtools) is not conditional; a custom tag is left out, a platform tag is conditional

records.title: Found by: review of #32.
records.description: Found by: review of #32. Line-anchored regexes written `^\s*…/m` (`usesMcp`, `sdkNames`, `mcpClient`, `sdkFile`, and eleven more in the Python, Go and Rust readers) were quadratic on runs of blank lines because `\s*` crosses newlines: 100 KB of newlines took about 50 s. They now use `^[ \t]*`; a Cargo feature array is read to at most 8 KB.

test.name: R-RD-19: 100 KB of blank lines is read in linear time (no ^\s*…/m regex crossing lines)

records.title: Found by: review of #32.
records.description: Found by: review of #32. A bare registrar whose server object is imported from another module (`from app.server import mcp`, or a relative import) was not followed. Imported server objects now count; the registrar's own registration is no longer counted as unresolved, and its tools' annotations are known (none) when that call is a plain statement with no `annotations=` or `**kwargs`. Review follow-up: a registrar also called outside a decorator (`create_tool(n, "D.")(f)`) keeps its own registration unresolved; annotations stay unknown when the registrar's body mentions annotations.

test.name: R-RD-20: a bare registrar on a server object imported from another module (from app.server import mcp) is followed
R-RD-20: a bare registrar's own registration is not an unresolved one, and annotations are known when its call is a plain statement
R-RD-20: a registrar also called outside a decorator keeps its registration unresolved; annotations set later in its body stay unknown

records.title: Found by: review of #32.
records.description: Found by: review of #32. A parenthesized multi-line import (`from fastmcp.tools import (\n tool,\n)`) was not seen as an SDK import, so `@tool` could go through the repository's own `tool()` factory. SDK names are now read from logical lines. Review follow-up: import names are split in code (a lazy capture before `\s*$` and `/\s+as\s+/`, in this PR and before it, were quadratic on a long run of spaces: 80,000 spaces took about 35 s).

test.name: R-RD-21: a parenthesized import over several lines (from fastmcp.tools import (\n tool,\n)) counts as the SDK's name
R-RD-21: an import line with a long run of spaces is read in linear time (Python and TypeScript)

records.title: Found by: review of #32.
records.description: Found by: review of #32. `importsMcpServer` looked for `import`, `const`, `let` and `var` without word boundaries, so `invariant` or `constructorArgs` after `McpServer` in one import hid it. The keywords are now matched as whole words.

test.name: R-RD-22: the import check finds McpServer when a later name in the same import contains "var", "let" or "const"

records.title: Found by: review of #32.
records.description: Found by: review of #32. `shadowAt` was quadratic for one def with many tool dict lines (and the guard walk and the per-line constant copy with it): 6,000 lines took about 6 s. test.name: R-RD-23: one def with many tool dict lines is read in linear time

records.title: Found by: review of #32.
records.description: Found by: review of #32. A folder named like `mcp-server-evals` was read, because only an exact `evals` folder was skipped (getsentry: a stand-in server under `packages/mcp-server-evals`). A folder with "evals" as a word of its name is now skipped like `evals`.

test.name: R-RD-24: a folder with "evals" as a word of its name (mcp-server-evals) is not read; medieval or retrievals is

records.title: Found by: loop upgrade 19 (review of sec-control-chars).
records.description: Found by: loop upgrade 19 (review of sec-control-chars). ESC was already flagged, but the message said only "Control characters.", so a server author could not tell an ANSI escape sequence (CSI, OSC, an OSC 8 hyperlink that relabels a link, a C1 byte) from a stray bell. The message now names the kinds and shows the sequences; no new check ID, so existing cases keep their reading. test.name: R-CHK-01: ESC sequences (CSI, OSC, OSC 8 hyperlink, C1) are named as ANSI terminal escape sequences, other controls stay listed

records.title: Found by: bench gap `gap-shell-injectable-url` (`real-world/cve-2025-6514-shape`, recall 0 of 1).
records.description: Found by: bench gap `gap-shell-injectable-url` (`real-world/cve-2025-6514-shape`, recall 0 of 1). No check flagged a URL with command substitution, a backtick command, `&&` or a newline then a command in metadata (the shape of CVE-2025-6514). records.title: Found by: loop upgrade 19 design (false-positive limits).
records.description: Found by: loop upgrade 19 design (false-positive limits). `;` or `|` in the address or path is attention; `&` parameters, `|` and `;` in a query, `;key=value` path parameters, entities, a closing code-span backtick, trailing punctuation and `${id}` templates must stay silent.

test.name: R-CHK-03: a ";" or "|" in the address or path is attention; in a query, as a matrix parameter, or in prose it is not read

records.title: Found by: loop upgrade 19 design (hostile-input rule).
records.description: Found by: loop upgrade 19 design (hostile-input rule). The ANSI and shell-URL scans use bounded quantifiers and one pass over scheme tokens; 200 KB of nested `a://`, `$`, backticks, `;`, ESC and OSC runs is read in linear time. Review of #37: the trailing-punctuation strip (`/[…]+$/`) was quadratic on a long run of `;` `.` `?` `*` followed by a letter (100,000 `;` then `a`: 5.9 s); it is now a backwards loop and R-CHK-04 covers those runs.

test.name: R-CHK-04: ANSI and shell-URL scans read hostile input in linear time

records.title: Found by: review of #37.
records.description: Found by: review of #37. The newline rule had the `i` flag and a wide metacharacter class, so prose after a URL fired blocking ("Open issues…", "Cat photos", "Node types", "Echo back", "Cmd+K", a code fence, `> quote`, `(see above)`, `$5 per call`). Command words are now lowercase and need an argument; only `$(`, a bare `;`, `|` or `&&` start a shell line.

test.name: R-CHK-05: a newline after a URL fires only before shell syntax (case-sensitive command words, no fence, quote, paren or price)

records.title: Found by: review of #37.
records.description: Found by: review of #37. A closing code-span backtick glued to a word (`` `https://x/items`s ``) and `&&` inside a query fired blocking; a pipe or semicolon between two URLs read as shell. Now attention, attention and not read; a backtick command and `&&` in the path stay blocking.

test.name: R-CHK-06: a glued closing backtick and "&&" in a query are attention, a backtick command and "&&" in the path stay blocking, and https://a|https://b is not read

records.title: Found by: loop upgrade 18 (taxonomy mapping).
records.description: Found by: loop upgrade 18 (taxonomy mapping). No record said which recognised test or risk IDs the checks touch, so a security buyer could not see coverage, and nothing would catch a new check with no mapping, a mapping for a removed check, or a mistyped ID. `docs/taxonomy/owasp-mcp.json` maps all checks to the OWASP MCP Security Testing Guide and MCP Top 10 (pinned by commit); `docs/TAXONOMY.md` is generated from it.

test.name: `test/taxonomy.test.mjs` › `R-TX-01: a check with no mapping entry, even an explicit none, fails`; `test/taxonomy.test.mjs` › `R-TX-01: a mapping entry that names a check that does not exist fails`; `test/taxonomy.test.mjs` › `R-TX-01: a test or item ID that is not in the pinned list fails`

records.title: live-probe oracle judge (new in this lane, found by its self test on GitHub before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle judge (new in this lane, found by its self test on GitHub before merge). The Go SDK client writes `idempotentHint: false` on a tool whose annotations leave it out (the spec default), so on kronicle-lite 0.10.2 its catalog hash differed from our reader's and the other three clients', and the judge raised two D4 `schema_mismatch` leads that would have fired on most servers with annotations. Catalogs are now also compared with the annotations that only state the spec default removed; such a client is recorded as `catalog_vs_reader: same_but_annotation_defaults`, with no disagreement.

test.name: R-ORC-01: a client SDK that writes out an annotation default (Go: idempotentHint false) is the same catalog, not a D4 disagreement; a real difference still is

records.title: live-probe oracle stage (found from its self test on GitHub before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle stage (found from its self test on GitHub before merge). The stage runs inside the sandbox driver's probe option, and the driver times its probe around that call, so `step_telemetry.probe_ms` held the oracle stage too (mcp-check: 12.4 s, of which about 1.2 s was the probe). The bundle now records `oracle_ms` and takes it out of `probe_ms`. The driver's own container record for the probe (raw telemetry) still spans both; corpus/LIVE-PROBE.md says so.

test.name: R-ORC-02: the driver's probe time holds the oracle stage (it runs inside the probe option); step_telemetry keeps the two apart

records.title: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge). A server could put a string of its choosing into `sdk_client_results.protocol_negotiated` and the results and control files outside raw/: the TypeScript 1.x client took the first `protocolVersion` in any message (a stray response with an unknown id is ignored by the SDK but was read by our tap), and the judge passed any 40 plain characters. The forgery control did not catch it (its marker is longer, and it echoes a real version). The tap now reads only the answer to our own initialize request, and the judge accepts only the specification's revisions, else `other`.

test.name: R-ORC-03: a server cannot put a string of its choosing into protocol_negotiated

records.title: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge). `runProgram` settled on `close`, which waits for every holder of the client's pipes: an orphaned `docker run` left by a killed client kept it open, so the session's container (on the fixed address) was never removed and the stage overran. Clients and suite runs are now process groups stopped whole at the limit, the session's container is removed at once, and the run settles on exit with a short grace.

test.name: R-ORC-04: a client whose child keeps its pipes open is still stopped at its limit, its whole process group with it, and its container removed at once

records.title: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge). The SDK clients run on the runner, outside the container's memory limit; a server writing gigabytes without a line break grew their heaps (a runner out-of-memory risk). Each client's server command now goes through `corpus/oracles/relay.mjs`: 24 MiB in all, 4 MiB a line.

test.name: R-ORC-05: what a server can send an oracle client on the runner is capped (relay.mjs): a flood without line breaks is stopped

records.title: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge). No `finally` around the conformance loop: an error skipped `bridge.close()`, leaving the live session's container on the fixed address while the driver went on; the stage's own cleanup could throw too. The bridge now closes in a `finally`, and cleanup errors are recorded, never thrown.

test.name: R-ORC-06: an error inside the conformance loop still closes the bridge, so no session container is left on the address

records.title: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge). Client and scenario limits ran to the budget less 5 s, plus up to about 40 s of kill, removal and trace wait, eating the reserve kept for the driver's second probe. Limits now keep 30 s of cleanup inside the budget. Also: the driver read a target without a limit as 300 s (the sandbox's default is 600 s), and HTTP targets got the oracle allowance though the stage never runs for them.

test.name: R-ORC-07: the stage keeps cleanup time inside its budget; the driver reads a target without a limit as 600 s; HTTP targets get no oracle allowance

records.title: live-probe oracle bridge (review, before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle bridge (review, before merge). One server process at a time was not enforced under concurrent requests: a second initialize arriving while the first closed the open session could start a second container (which then fails on the fixed address). Starting and ending sessions now take turns.

test.name: R-ORC-08: two initialize requests at once still leave one server process

test.name: R-ORC-09: a check id repeated in a scenario takes its worst status; a client that crashed is D12

records.title: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge).
records.description: live-probe oracle stage (review, before merge).
