The self test now refuses an unavailable client (the control still tolerates an install outage, recorded as our fault), and both records are kept in raw/ and timed.

test.name: R-ORC-10: the self test refuses a client that did not install; both oracle records of a target are kept and timed

records.title: Found by: loop findings of 27 Nov (RUNNING-LANES section G).
records.description: Found by: loop findings of 27 Nov (RUNNING-LANES section G). The Go client decoded `tools/list` into go-sdk v1.8.0's typed `mcp.Tool` and re-marshalled it, which drops `execution` (no such field), annotation keys the SDK does not know (`returnDirect`, `description`), an empty annotations title and hints a server put at the tool's top level, and writes `readOnlyHint` and `idempotentHint` out: 534 results (127 subjects) of 25-27 Nov carried `D4 catalog reader client:go`, 503 for `execution` alone, and the analyst's projection made 514 of 522 readable ones identical. The client now taps its connection under the SDK and reports each `tools/list` result as the server sent it (`tools_source: wire`), keeping the typed parse for the outcome and its count (`typed_tool_count`); the judge compares a list reported only from the typed structs (`tools_source: typed`) on names, never on its catalog (`sdk_typed_only`), and is never the reference the other clients' catalogs are compared with. Mutation-checked: with the Go client back on its typed output, or the judge ignoring `tools_source`, the test fails.

test.name: R-ORC-11: the Go client reports the tools/list result the server sent, not its SDK's typed re-marshal; the same catalog is same, a typed-only list is never a D4

records.title: Found by: loop findings of 27 Nov (RUNNING-LANES finding 9 and finding 3).
records.description: Found by: loop findings of 27 Nov (RUNNING-LANES finding 9 and finding 3). The clients-only pass ran on every probe that got no list, also when the server never started: 769 skipped results of 25-27 Nov ran it (1.9 h of 26.7 h of job time), 600 of them servers that exited before initialize, and every client failed initialize too. It now runs only when the server answered the probe (an initialize result, or a 2026-07-28 refusal of it); otherwise the record is `mode: skipped`, `why: not_started`, and a later probe that gets an answer still runs it. A server that declared no tools capability (live-probe R-LP-75) gave a D6 per client although the clients agreed (TypeScript v2 lists an empty list, the others are refused): such clients now agree with the reader (`catalog_vs_reader: no_tools_capability`). Mutation-checked: with the answer check or the no-tools agreement off, the test fails.

test.name: R-ORC-12: no oracle clients for a target that never answered (the skip says why); a server with no tools capability gives no disagreement

records.title: Found by: owner decision of 27 Nov (design D1, OWNER-NOTES §3): the oracle stage had the four SDK clients and the conformance suite but not the MCP Inspector, the tool most server authors check their…
records.description: Found by: owner decision of 27 Nov (design D1, OWNER-NOTES §3): the oracle stage had the four SDK clients and the conformance suite but not the MCP Inspector, the tool most server authors check their server with. `@modelcontextprotocol/inspector` 2.16.0 is now pinned (pins.json, the npm lockfile; no other package moved) and runs as a fifth client in its CLI mode (`--cli --method tools/list`) through `corpus/oracles/inspector-client.mjs`, whose pass-through tells a refused initialize from a refused list and reads the protocol (the Inspector reports neither). Its list is compared on the specification's Tool and ToolAnnotations keys only (`catalog: spec_fields`, `same_spec_fields`), since its own parse drops other keys, and it is never the reference client; its disagreements are recorded like the SDK clients', and an Inspector-only failure adds no skip and no fault. Mutation-checked: with the field projection off, with any answer id counted, or with the stage ignored, the test fails. Review of #61: the reference client is never the Inspector, also when it comes first in the clients list (a case with a mutation check of the guard), and an Inspector failure is shown to add no skip to the live-probe record (the item stays graded, fault none), not by an assertion that could not fail.

test.name: R-ORC-13: the MCP Inspector is an oracle client: its answer in the clients' format, compared on the specification's fields, its failures disagreements and never the server's fault

records.title: Found by: review of #61 (latent).
records.description: Found by: review of #61 (latent). The Inspector starts its stdio server with a default environment of its own (HOME, LOGNAME, PATH, SHELL, TERM, USER), so the server command behind it (the `docker run -i` of the target's container) lost the DOCKER_* variables `oracleEnv` gives the client: a sandbox on DOCKER_HOST, DOCKER_CONTEXT or DOCKER_CONFIG would fail initialize on every item and flood `oracle_disagreements`. The client writes the environment it was given, less DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG (registry credentials), to a file of its own (mode 600) in the session folder and the pass-through (`--pipe <state> <env file> -- <command>`) starts the server command with it; without that file it does not start it. Mutation check included.

test.name: R-ORC-14: the server command behind the Inspector gets the client's environment (DOCKER_* included), not the Inspector's default one

records.title: Found by: reader-gap cases (Rust `#[schemars(transform = f)]`, about 105 registry repos).
records.description: Found by: reader-gap cases (Rust `#[schemars(transform = f)]`, about 105 registry repos). The `transform` key of `#[schemars]` was skipped without a mark, at field and container level, so the untransformed schema was listed as the SDK's: `["T","null"]` where docling.rs's `drop_null` leaves `"T"`, `type` unions where org-mcp-server's `nullable_as_any_of` writes `anyOf`, no `pattern` where weather-bridge's `city_query_schema` inserts one. A transform is now followed when its body matches a known transform token for token (its own names aside) or only inserts keys whose values are literals, constants or `format!` of them; any other keeps the tool, marks its input schema not readable and names the function (`schema-transform`). Fixtures trimmed from the three repositories (`test/repos/rust-transform/`). Second review: `transform = other_mod::f` was looked up by its last name only, so a same-file `f` was taken for it; the path is now kept, resolves to that module's file (`src/other_mod.rs`, `src/other_mod/mod.rs`, `crate::…` from the crate root, `self::` this file), and `super::` or a path that names no module file is declined.

records.title: Found by: reader-gap cases (FastAPI-derived tools, about 46 registry repos).
records.description: Found by: reader-gap cases (FastAPI-derived tools, about 46 registry repos). A server built with `FastMCP.from_fastapi(app, route_maps=…)` or `route_map_fn=…` gave "no tool definitions found": FastAPI routes, routers, prefixes and route maps were not read (FalkorDB/QueryWeaver, sveinbjornt/ensk.is, Xyber-Labs/mcp-servers). The app's included routers are now followed and the route maps applied, each tool listed as FastMCP names, describes and flattens it; a map or router the reader cannot resolve leaves those routes out with the reason in the provenance, and a parameter or body it cannot type marks the input schema not readable. Second review: names were listed as certain for any FastMCP version, a described path parameter's description was trusted with no version known, "no route map matches means TOOL" was applied to versions before 2.8.0 (where `DEFAULT_ROUTE_MAPPINGS` made GET routes resources; checked in FastMCP's `src/fastmcp/server/openapi.py` at v2.7.1 and v2.8.0), a route map `pattern` was handed to JavaScript as written (`\Z`, `\A`, inline flags, possessive quantifiers read differently; `(a+)+` can backtrack without end), and an absolute import could resolve to another package of a monorepo. Names are now certain only for the versions the fixtures checked (2.14.5, 4.1.6, 4.1.7), otherwise marked with a note; with no version known a described path parameter leaves the description unread; a range allowing a version before 2.8.0 leaves out GET routes no map decides; a pattern JavaScript would read differently, or over 200 characters, makes the route maps unreadable; imports resolve only under the server file's package root.

R-RD-37: no route maps (Tavily shape, fastmcp 2.x): every route of routers included in a loop over an imported list is a tool; header alias, Field constraints, generated summary and operation id

R-RD-37: a route map by tag and method decides per route; a router the reader cannot find is named, its routes left out

records.title: Found by: reader-gap research (sample of registry repos read as "no tool definitions found").
records.description: Found by: reader-gap research (sample of registry repos read as "no tool definitions found"). Tools registered through a project helper defined in another file of the repository and imported by a relative import (`registerTool(server, name, config, cb)`, `registerTool(server, name, description, shape, cb)`, `registerTool(server, tool)`) were not read: helpers were found only in the file of their calls, and even there a helper named `registerTool`, one with type parameters (`function registerTool<T>(`), one that casts what it forwards (`config as never`), one that forwards to `server.tool(...)`, or one that forwards properties of a parameter (`tool.name`) was not recognised (clssck/dataiku_mcp, anoopt/outlook-meetings-scheduler-mcp-server, mauricio-cantu/brasil-api-mcp-server: exit 3). Such helpers are now followed across one relative import; a call in a loop over a known collection is read once per element; a call whose name cannot be worked out is counted as unresolved. A call whose description argument cannot be read (`getDesc()`) took the description's place as the shape and lost the real one; the description is now marked unread and the shape read from its own argument (unread too when that is the callback).

records.description:
Found by: reader-gap research (runtime-built registries). A registry of tool definitions in another module was not read where it is iterated to register: a typed constant (`export const getCepTool: McpToolDefinition

= {...}`) was not collected, because the type annotation was skipped past its `=`, and a loop over a collection was unrolled only when the collection was declared in the same file (mauricio-cantu/brasil-api-mcp-server: exit 3; `for (const def of TOOLS) server.registerTool(def.id, { description: def.summary, ... })` with TOOLS imported: 0 tools and 1 unresolved). Typed constants are now collected, and a constant imported by one relative import from the file that declares it is unrolled when neither file changes it; a registry its module changes is still counted as unresolved. Second review: "frozen" was decided from the declaring file alone, so `export const TOOLS = [alpha]` with `TOOLS.push(beta)` in a third module gave `[alpha]` and nothing unresolved. Every file that imports the constant (under any name, through re-exports, `export *` or a namespace) must now only read it: a mutator call, an assignment, `++`/`--`, `= NAME`, the name handed to a call other than `Object.entries/keys/values/freeze`, or a `require()`/`import()` of its module makes the loop unresolved. The check runs only at a loop that needs it, memoized per (declaring file, name).

R-RD-33: typed tool objects exported by other files (const t: ToolDefinition

= {…}), listed and registered with forEach through an imported helper, are read

R-RD-33: an object map imported from another module and iterated with Object.entries is read, the key as the name

R-RD-33: a registry that other modules only read (length, for…of, Object.keys, ns.TOOLS.length) is still unrolled

records.description: Found by: reader-gap research (runtime-built registries). `for tool in tools: mcp.add_tool(tool)` over a list of the file's functions was skipped without a trace, since the loop variable is not a def of the file (stefanoamorelli/sec-edgar-mcp: exit 3, 21 tools). The loop is now followed when its items are a list or tuple literal of the file's defs, written in the loop or assigned once and not changed; each function is read as `mcp.add_tool(fn)` is. A loop over anything else is counted as an unresolved registration. Second review: a module-level list was followed although another module could change it (`from server import tools; tools.append(f)`), and a function of the same file appending to it was missed when the loop was inside another function. A module-level list is now not followed when another Python file that imports it, or its module, appends to it, changes it in place, rebinds it or hands it to a call, nor when any line of the file changes it.

R-RD-34: a module-level list of functions another module changes (append, extend, insert, rebind, handed to a call) is counted as unresolved

records.description: Found by: reader-gap cases (zod helpers: isokron-ai/mcp-check, barzoj/somtoday-mcp). `.regex(/…/)` on a zod string was read without its `pattern`, in a chain and in a union branch, so every pattern constraint was missing from the derived list. It is now written as the RegExp's source (flags not carried, as the SDK's converters do); two or more regexes, which the SDK puts in `allOf`, leave it out. Dropping the flags is deliberate: zod 4's `toJSONSchema` and zod-to-json-schema with its default options (no `applyRegexFlags`) both write only the source, so `/^[a-z]+$/i` is listed as `^[a-z]+$`.

records.description: Found by: reader-gap cases (zod helpers: isokron-ai/mcp-check). `.max(SECTIONS.length)` lost `maxItems` silently: a property path into a constant array was not read, and a bound that was not a plain number was skipped without marking the schema inexact. Arithmetic of literal constants (`MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024`, `MAX_BYTES / 1048576` in a description) was not read either. Bounds and numbers now take number literals, literal constants, `.length` of a constant array or string read whole, and `+ - * / %` of those; anything else is left out and marks the schema inexact. Second review: a number was also taken from a `let` or `var` (`let M = 5; M = 10; .max(M)` gave 5); the collector now records the declaration kind, and only a `const` gives a bound, an operand or text.

records.description: Found by: reader-gap cases (zod helpers: CruGlobal/flightdeck-mcp-server, barzoj/somtoday-mcp). Unions and `.nullable()` were written one way for every zod version: a union of primitives as `anyOf` (both SDK converters list a type array), `.nullable()` of a union was lost, and `.nullable()` of a constrained schema was merged into a type array. They now follow zod-to-json-schema for zod 3 and zod's own `toJSONSchema` for zod 4, with the type-array compaction only from zod 4.5.0 (`detectSdk` returns the zod version). Checked against SDK 1.29.0 with zod 3.25.76 and SDK 1.32.2 with zod 4.3.6 and 4.6.7. Second review: a zod 3 union whose options carried a wrapper (`z.union([z.string().optional(), z.number()])`, `.refine()`, `.transform(Number)`) was written as a type array, which zod-to-json-schema keeps for unions of bare, unchecked primitives only; an option wrapped by `.optional()`, `.nullish()`, `.refine()`, `.superRefine()`, `.transform()`, `.brand()`, `.readonly()`, `.catch()`, `.pipe()` or `.default()`, or with a hidden check (`.trim()`), now makes the union `anyOf` (inexact for `.optional()`/`.nullish()`, which the converter wraps in `anyOf [{not: {}}, …]`), and `.nullable()` of a wrapped schema is `anyOf` with null.

test.name: R-RD-28: zod 3 writes a union of bare primitives as a type array, and .nullable() of anything else as anyOf with null
R-RD-28: zod 3 writes a union with a wrapped or checked option as anyOf, never a type array
R-RD-28: zod 4 writes .nullable() as anyOf with null, and from zod 4.5.0 compacts an anyOf of bare types to a type array

records.description: Found by: QA-40 (repro r1, k8s-flux159@f93604a `explain_resource` and `list_api_resources`). An exec whose program is a parameter of a guard wrapper was `definite` ("command is not a literal") although every caller passed `"kubectl"` and a read-only sub-command. records.description: Found by: QA-40 (repro r2, mysql-designcomputer@943ce83 `get_schema_info` and `get_table_sample`). An SSH tunnel `Popen` whose argv comes only from constants and environment variables, after `if not ssh: yield; return` in a context manager, was `definite`. The file/HTTP target rule (R-AE-27) now applies to exec: no argument of the tool in the argv is `may` ("the command does not come from the tool's arguments"); the data flow also follows `push`/`append`/`extend` onto a list. After an early `return` inside an `if` whose condition no argument reaches, the rest of the function is on a conditional path; a guard on the arguments (validation) is not. `ts-sinks/exec_rm` (`execSync('rm -rf build')`, a constant command) moves to the known misses of R-AE-16.

records.description: Found by: the QA-40 re-run of this series (word-gongrzhe@a3bbbb6). `with open(filepath, 'a'): pass` (word-gongrzhe `check_file_writeable`, a check that the file is not locked) was a `definite` write on 38 tools once submodule calls were followed. records.description: Found by: loop findings 27 Nov (scan-static against live-probe: KallistoX/mcp-unifi-applications@cec2194, Thecimal/quantified-self-mcp@5419726, alexgaoth/escalate-anything@847cf77). `ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, ...)` was listed snake_case unless an `mcp>=2` pin was the first manifest line the reader met, so `spec-annotation-key-case` fired and `anthropic-hint` / `openai-hints-explicit` read no hints (spec D, Anthropic F) on servers whose live list is camelCase. The installed SDK major is now worked out the way a resolver does: a `uv.lock` entry for mcp decides; else the highest major every requirement on mcp and fastmcp allows (fastmcp 4.x needs mcp 2.x, earlier lines 1.x; keywords and classifiers are not requirements), narrowed by the SDK modules the source imports (`mcp.server.mcpserver` is 2.x only, `mcp.server.fastmcp` 1.x only). Under 2.x the hints are listed camelCase and keys that are not fields are dropped (`extra="ignore"`); under 1.x they stay as written (`extra="allow"`); with no knowable major the snake_case hints are left out, the annotations marked not readable and the reason given in the candidate's notes.

R-RD-40: with no knowable SDK major, snake_case hints are left out and the annotations marked not readable, with the reason; camelCase keys stay
R-RD-40: requirement specifiers: the highest major every requirement allows; keywords and classifiers are not requirements

records.description: Found by: loop findings 27 Nov (Panelica/panelica-mcp@88a96e9 graded on 490 tools, live 37; dsanchezp18/maplestats-mcp@d20a8a6 graded on 514, live 3). A committed list ranked first as `exact` even when it was a backend catalogue the server searches and calls into, and registrations behind a FastMCP tool search transform were graded as the list, so Anthropic, OpenAI and security grades were given for tools the server does not list. A committed list is now taken for the server's list only when it lists every tool the source registers (or no registration was read); otherwise it ranks after the source list, `hints.listNotUsed` records it and the source candidate's notes say why. A FastMCP search transform (`fastmcp.server.transforms.search` or `jev_search`, or a subclass, given to `transforms=` or `add_transform`) makes the scan incomplete with the reason, and nothing is graded. A name with a part the reader could not work out (shown as "…") is never listed: the registration counts as unresolved.

records.title: Found by: second review of PR 58.
records.description: Found by: second review of PR 58. The Python SDK major was one answer for the whole repository: the first `uv.lock` with an mcp entry decided for every package, so a package with `mcp>=2` was read on another folder's 1.x lock and blamed with `spec-annotation-key-case`. It is now worked out per package folder: the file's own folder or the nearest one above it with a pyproject.toml, requirements file or lock; a lock there or above (a workspace root) decides; manifests under examples/, docs/, tests/ and the like count only for their own folder; packages that disagree leave the repository-level answer unknown. Also: `poetry.lock` and `requirements.lock` are read, environment markers are kept (a marker that changes the major gives unknown, with the reason), a major read from an open range is named in the notes, and a search transform's reason is kept when over-budget candidates are counted too. Second review: only runtime requirements decide (project.dependencies, the main Poetry table, requirements files other than dev/test/docs ones); a dependency group or extra that would install another major leaves it unknown; a lock the nearest folder's runtime requirements do not allow (a parent project's, or stale) leaves it unknown; and a package whose own manifest is in the listing but was not read is not decided by an ancestor's lock.

test.name: R-RD-44: a lock or requirement counts for the package folder that holds it: one package's mcp 1.x lock never decides for another's mcp>=2
R-RD-44: requirements under examples/ or docs/ never decide for the server; an environment marker that changes the major gives unknown; a major read from a range says so
R-RD-44: a search transform keeps its reason when over-budget candidates are also counted
R-RD-44: only runtime dependencies decide the SDK major; a dependency group or extra that would install another major leaves it unknown
R-RD-44: a lock the nearest folder's requirements do not allow (a parent project's, or stale) leaves the SDK major unknown
R-RD-44: a package whose own manifest was not read (past the reader's limits) is not decided by an ancestor's lock

records.description: **Finding (containment):** a target's work volume had no disk or inode cap. Named Docker volumes sat on the runner's own disk, so an install or server that wrote without end (an archive bomb, a fill, one `fallocate`) could fill it, and with it the shard's results and the targets after it. `install-runsc.sh` now mounts Docker's volumes folder as an ext4 file of its own (`volume_fs_mb` 6144, `volume_fs_inodes` 1,048,576 in `gvisor.json`, reserved up front and formatted with `nodiscard` so the reservation holds, mounted before any volume exists), and the strict preflight refuses a host without it. records.description: Pulled target images had no disk cap: a layer that unpacks without end would fill the runner's disk. Docker's whole data-root now lives on a filesystem of its own (`docker_root` /var/lib/isokron-docker, `docker_fs_mb` 20480, `docker_fs_inodes` 2,097,152, reserved up front), with the volumes filesystem (R-SBX-23) inside it, and the containerd image store pinned off so images stay on it (overlay2). The strict preflight checks the data-root, overlay2, both filesystems' inode counts, and that each image file is fully reserved (no holes: a discard or a trim would hand its blocks back); fstrim's timer is stopped. On GitHub the first version lost 512 MB of the data-root's reservation within seconds, which the hole check caught: it was the inode tables, which the kernel's lazy init zeroes after the mount with write-zeroes requests that a loop device turns into holes. mkfs now writes the inode tables and journal itself (`lazy_itable_init=0,lazy_journal_init=0`); both are also mounted `nodiscard`, and the preflight refuses one mounted with discard. From the review of pull request 11.

records.description: Found by: mcp-check's review of every recorded live-probe start failure (26 Nov). Every server ran with `--workdir /tmp`, an OCI image's too, so an image whose entrypoint or files are relative to its own WORKDIR failed: `Cannot find module '/tmp/dist/index.js'`, `can't open file '/tmp/server.py'`, `dotnet` not finding its DLL. 11 were recorded as our limit, 6 as the server's crash and 25 as the server needing credentials. An OCI target now runs in its image's WORKDIR, read from the pulled image (`docker image inspect`, data only); `/tmp` when it sets none, and always for npm, PyPI and Go. A working folder that is not a plain absolute path (no `.` or `..` segment) is refused.

test.name: R-SBX-44 an OCI target runs in its image's own WORKDIR, read from the pulled image, never one it cannot name plainly

records.title: 8 OCI servers wrote to a VOLUME their image declares (`/data`, `/config`, `/var/log/supervisor`) and hit the read-only root as uid 65534.
records.description: 8 OCI servers wrote to a VOLUME their image declares (`/data`, `/config`, `/var/log/supervisor`) and hit the read-only root as uid 65534. Each declared VOLUME now gets a tmpfs (`rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec`, 32 MiB, mode 1777), at most 8 (with `/tmp`, at most half the memory limit: tmpfs is memory), never over `/tmp`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/etc` or our own `/work` and `/opt`; the root stays read-only and `sandboxRunArgs` refuses any path `volumeTmpfs` would drop.

test.name: R-SBX-45 a size-capped tmpfs over each VOLUME the image declares, at most eight, never over /tmp or the system folders

records.title: Found by: security review of #14.
records.description: Found by: security review of #14. An image WORKDIR under `/proc`, `/sys` or `/dev` (`/proc/self/fd/7`, the Leaky Vessels shape; not exploitable under runsc) passed `imagePath` and became `--workdir`. It is refused in `imageConfigOf` and `sandboxRunArgs`, recorded as `workdir_refused` (printable, cut to 120), and the server runs in `/tmp`; mcp-check reads that run as our limit. `WORKDIR /` (postgres:16-alpine) is no kernel folder and is used as is (verification of #14: it was refused and mislabelled).

test.name: R-SBX-50 a WORKDIR under /proc, /sys or /dev is refused, recorded, and the server runs in /tmp instead

records.title: Found by: security review of #14.
records.description: Found by: security review of #14. A tmpfs over a VOLUME hides whatever the image ships there: images with `VOLUME /app`, `/config` or a bin folder that started before would fail and be blamed. A VOLUME equal to or holding the WORKDIR or the entrypoint's folder is left out (`holds_code`), and of the rest only folders that are empty in the image get one: a created, never started container (no network, entrypoint `/surface-never-runs`) and the head of `docker cp <c>:<path> -`, read as tar headers only; a file, a link (one to `/etc` could hide our resolv.conf) or any entry means no tmpfs. What was left out and why is recorded (`volumes_dropped`, `volume_seeded`). The probe container goes with `rm -f -v`, so no anonymous volume is left per VOLUME (verification of #14).

test.name: R-SBX-51 no tmpfs over a VOLUME that holds the image's code or ships content: only empty folders get one, the rest are recorded
R-SBX-51 volumeContent creates, reads and removes the probe container with its anonymous volumes (rm -f -v)

records.title: Found by: the search for the cause of R-SBX-54 (it was not that cause).
records.description: Found by: the search for the cause of R-SBX-54 (it was not that cause). The egress proxy destroyed a tunnel's client side as soon as the server closed; a client that still sent (a TLS close_notify) got a reset, which on Linux and in gVisor's netstack discards the bytes it had not yet read (a server that answers and closes at once, as github.com does after a 302). Each side is now ended after its buffered bytes are written and destroyed only after LINGER_MS. Mutation check (Linux) included.

test.name: R-SBX-53 egress proxy: a server that sends its answer and closes at once is passed on whole, never reset, also when the client still sends

records.title: Found by: the MCP bundle measurement of mcp-check #53 (every bundle download failed in 2 s with ECONNRESET).
records.description: Found by: the MCP bundle measurement of mcp-check #53 (every bundle download failed in 2 s with ECONNRESET). `sandbox/mcpb-fetch.mjs` made its GET with `agent: false`, so Node handed it to a fresh Agent that ignored the tunnel socket and connected by itself, by name, past the proxy; in the sandbox the name lookup answers with the network logger, which reset it, so it failed closed. The options carry no agent, and state port 443 and the Host header (without them Node writes `Host: github.com:80`, which github.com redirects to itself). Mutation checks included.

test.name: R-SBX-54 the bundle download goes over the proxy's tunnel only: no agent of Node's (which would connect by itself, past the proxy), port 443 and the Host header stated

The layer is mounted `volume-nocopy`. Mutation checks included (`nosuid,nodev` dropped).

records.title: `Docker.writableLayer` makes a fresh upper volume (one that exists is refused), gives its upper folder to 65534 at 0750 with a root helper that has CAP_CHOWN only (under runsc, no network), reads eac…
records.description: `Docker.writableLayer` makes a fresh upper volume (one that exists is refused), gives its upper folder to 65534 at 0750 with a root helper that has CAP_CHOWN only (under runsc, no network), reads each volume's folder back from `docker volume inspect` and refuses one Docker keeps anywhere but its data-root, makes the overlay volume, reads its driver and options back and refuses any but exactly ours, and has a 65534 helper see the work volume through it (read-only) before a server may use it: a layer the kernel refuses is our failure, never the server's. `dropLayer` removes the overlay volume, then its upper volume, never with `-f` (which drops Docker's record of a volume it failed to remove and leaves the data unlisted on the volume filesystem), the upper one only once the overlay volume is gone (never an upperdir a mounted overlay uses), and returns `{ removed, error }`; the work volume stays. The sweep removes layer volumes first, without `-f`, and leaves upper volumes alone while one is still there (review of #17). Mutation checks included (Mountpoint check, options read-back, the check helper, the chown, `-f`, the upper removed after a failure, the sweep's order).

test.name: R-SBX-58 a layer: a fresh upper volume made 65534's by a root helper with CAP_CHOWN only, the overlay volume with exactly our options read back, a check through it; removed whole, and said so
R-SBX-58 a layer is refused when Docker keeps a volume anywhere but its data-root, when the overlay's options are not ours, or when the check through it fails
R-SBX-58 an overlay volume Docker will not remove keeps its upper volume (never an upperdir a mounted overlay uses), and says so; the sweep removes layers first, without -f

records.title: `bin/run-shard.mjs` takes `writableWork` (main's option, or `--writable-work`; true or false, off by default): each server probe of a package kind (npm, pypi, go, cargo, nuget, mcpb; never an OCI tar…
records.description: `bin/run-shard.mjs` takes `writableWork` (main's option, or `--writable-work`; true or false, off by default): each server probe of a package kind (npm, pypi, go, cargo, nuget, mcpb; never an OCI target, which has no work volume) gets a fresh layer of its own at `/work` and a `/data` tmpfs, and after the probe its container goes, then its layer, before the next probe's layer is made: nothing the bare probe wrote reaches the env probe, the next target, or the work volume the lock read-out reads. A layer that cannot be made is recorded (`writable_work.probes.<tag>.error`) and that probe runs on the read-only volume; one Docker will not remove is recorded as `removed: false` with `remove_error` and in `errors`. This is what keeps a server off the work volume itself (R-SBX-60's settings check only compares a container with its manifest). Records carry `writable_work`, `shard.json` `writable_work`. Mutation checks included (no removal, the work volume itself read-write, one layer for both probes, on by default, the removal error dropped).

test.name: R-SBX-59 with writableWork, each server probe of a package kind gets a fresh layer of its own at /work and a /data tmpfs, removed before the next; the work volume stays read-only to everything else; off by default, never for an OCI target
R-SBX-59 a layer that cannot be made is recorded and the probe runs on the read-only work volume, as without the option
R-SBX-59 a layer Docker will not remove is recorded as not removed, with the error, and its upper volume is left for the sweep

records.title: A server with the layer keeps every other setting (gVisor, 65534, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only root, limits); `/data` is a tmpfs exactly like an image VOLUME's (`noexec,nosuid,nodev`…
records.description: A server with the layer keeps every other setting (gVisor, 65534, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only root, limits); `/data` is a tmpfs exactly like an image VOLUME's (`noexec,nosuid,nodev`, 32 MiB), and the tmpfs rules still refuse `/work`, `/opt`, `/etc`, `/tmp` paths. The guard's settings check (`inspectMismatches`) accepts the layer at `/work` as declared and still refuses a bind of the work volume's host folder, a container whose mounts differ from its manifest (the work volume read-write where the manifest names the layer), a writable root and `-v` binds; what keeps the manifest itself from naming the work volume read-write is R-SBX-59. Isolation does not rest on `nosuid`/`noexec` (runsc may ignore them, R-CASE-28): it rests on gVisor, 65534, no capabilities and no-new-privileges, as for `/tmp`. Mutation checks included (`/data` exec, the mount check relaxed).

test.name: R-SBX-60 a server with the layer keeps every other setting; /data is a tmpfs like an image VOLUME's; the guard's settings check accepts the layer and still refuses a host path, the bare work volume or a writable root

records.title: Found by: review of #17.
records.description: Found by: review of #17. On the local lane the preflight is not strict, so nothing checked that Docker's volumes folder is the capped filesystem `install-runsc.sh` makes (`dockerFsProblem`); with `writableWork` on such a host a server could fill the runner's own disk through its layer. The option is now refused, a harness error before any target, on every lane unless `dockerFsProblem(cfg)` is null; without the option the local lane runs as before. Mutation checks included (no check, the check on the ci lane only).

test.name: R-SBX-61 writableWork is refused on every lane unless Docker's volumes are their own capped filesystem: the local lane's preflight does not check it

records.description: install-git-submodule: on the install network (node24-build, git 2.39), a superproject whose submodules point at an `ext::` transport (a command of ours that would leave a mark), a `file://` path and an outside host (`sub.evil.example`), cloned with `--recurse-submodules`, and an npm git dependency on another (`npm.evil.example`). `ext::` never runs and `file://` is not followed: git's own defaults, which the sandbox keeps in force by refusing GIT_ names in a target's environment (R-MUT-07). The proxy refuses both outside hosts, and that is the control: each host is asked for only by a submodule update or by npm, so both refusals show everything was tried (on GitHub a first version passed with no submodules at all, because `git add .` had taken the hand-made gitlinks out again). records.description: Found by: loop gates review (the disk cap added to the sandbox in mcp-surface-corpus #11, R-SBX-23). The hand-dispatched batch path (`corpus-batch.yml`, `corpus/run-shard.mjs`) had its own sandbox: a target's work volume was plain Docker volume space on the runner's disk, so an install or server that wrote without end (an archive bomb, one `fallocate`) could fill the runner and lose the shard's results. The workflow now runs the pinned `sandbox-guard` action (the same commit as `corpus.yml`) before the target list is decrypted, which puts Docker's data, volumes and logs on capped filesystems and puts up the sandbox firewall; `run-ci-shard.sh` passes `--require-volume-cap`, and the driver then refuses to start unless `<data root>/volumes` is a loop-mounted ext4 of its own (`volumeCapProblem`). The driver itself still runs targets under runc; this path is to be retired (loop/README.md, "The older corpus path").

test.name: R-WC-10: the CI lane refuses to run unless Docker's volumes folder is a capped filesystem of its own

records.description: Found by: loop gates review (R-SBX-24 of mcp-surface-corpus #11). The loop worker's collector (`loop/sandbox/collect.mjs`) walked `/work/out` without links but `readdirSync` on the root itself followed a link a target had planted there or above it. It now reads its root only when `realpath` equals the path, else prints `{"error":"root_is_a_link"}` and exits 3, so the driver collects nothing for that step. records.title: Found by: review of tool-qa#66 (switching the writecheck lane on).
records.description: Found by: review of tool-qa#66 (switching the writecheck lane on). With setup_minutes 8 the pump's lease is 52 min, but `loop/run-items.mjs` let the item running at the 26-minute shard deadline go 15 more minutes, so items plus prepare and teardown could pass the job's 45-minute timeout-minutes and the job would be killed before the shard's bundles were sealed and uploaded. The grace is now `ITEM_GRACE_MS` (5 min); review found the host-side work around the items (up to ~15 min before t0, overhang and sealing after) could still pass 45, so the shard budget is 20 min (was 26), timeout-minutes 50, and tool-qa's setup_minutes 12 (lease 58). The test reads the exported constants and checks the call site uses the grace constant.

test.name: R-WC-13: the last item cannot outlast the writecheck job or the pump lease

records.description: The PostgreSQL cells had no known answer: nothing showed that they could catch a lost update, an unfiltered delete or a dropped idempotency key against a real PostgreSQL, or that the correct build holds. Found by: the protection-off runs of this change (each defect is the protection switched off). Review of #68: in CI (`CI` with `CLI_DIR`, or `PG_LIVE_REQUIRED`) a skipped live test fails, so the `pg-fixture` job cannot pass with nothing run; the control channel compares its bearer token in constant time and answers a refused value with 4xx, not 500.

R-WC-17: known bad (lost-update): the PostgreSQL cells catch it as MWS-CONC-2 on delete_item, and the run still completes
R-WC-17: known bad (empty-filter-deletes-all): the PostgreSQL cells catch it as MWS-TGT-2 on delete_items, and the run still completes

records.title: A fixture whose server talks to Redis would normally pull in a client library, and with it a dependency tree that a person has to trust.
records.description: A fixture whose server talks to Redis would normally pull in a client library, and with it a dependency tree that a person has to trust. redis-tracker has none: its client is `src/resp.mjs` (RESP2), the lockfile holds only the package, and the loader refuses a changed byte of `src/` (`source.sha256`), a new file there, a dependency in the lock, an install script and a lock from another host. A test reads every import of the source and allows only `node:` modules and the folder's own files. The defect builds, the manifest's header and the known answers in `fixtures.json` name the same four builds, and the source has the WATCH and the `SET ... NX` that the defects switch off.

test.name: R-WC-19: redis-tracker is a source fixture with no dependency: its folder is pinned by digest, its Redis client is its own
R-WC-19: a changed byte of the fixture, a dependency, a loosened lock or a lost label is refused (mutations)
R-WC-19: the defects of the server, the manifest's comment and fixtures.json's known answers name the same builds

records.title: npm has no maintained carrier of a `redis-server` binary and the sandbox's install network reaches registry.npmjs.org only, so the backend's executable had to come from somewhere else without trustin…
records.description: npm has no maintained carrier of a `redis-server` binary and the sandbox's install network reaches registry.npmjs.org only, so the backend's executable had to come from somewhere else without trusting a tag. It comes from a digest-pinned official image used as a file source: `fixtures.json` `binary_image` pins the image by tag and index digest and, per platform, three files by path and sha256 (`redis-server` and the two OpenSSL libraries it links); the driver creates a container of the image without starting it, copies the files out, checks each sha256 and mounts them read-only; the backend checks the same sha256 values again (a test keeps the two lists equal) and refuses a server that does not measure as the pinned version. The copied set is proved complete: the ELF NEEDED entries of `redis-server` (and of the copied libraries) are read in process, and each must be a pinned copied file or one of `system_libs` (the sandbox image's own); a mount may not be one of the container's own folders or another fixture's. Mutations: an image without a digest or from another registry, a mount over the tools, a missing platform or file, a malformed pin, and a copied file that is not the pinned one (refused, the container removed, never started). mcp-surface-corpus is unchanged.

test.name: R-WC-20: the backend binary is pinned twice, by the image's digest and by sha256 of each file, and the two pins agree
R-WC-20: the image reference and the file pins are validated; a wrong file is refused before it is kept (mutations)
R-WC-20: every shared library redis-server needs is a pinned copied file or one of the sandbox image's (ELF NEEDED, read in process)

A proposed hash next to an accepted one, or a malformed one, is refused.

R-WC-22: the plan a person accepted is in the repository and is the one fixtures.json names; a proof item never counts as an acceptance

records.title: The Redis cells had no known answer.

records.title: Found by: tool-qa R-COV-01 (coverage gaps go first).
records.description: Found by: tool-qa R-COV-01 (coverage gaps go first). The worker's skips said no fault side, so ingest recorded each reason's default: `unknown` for `no_runnable_artifact`, `timeout_start` and `install_failed_registry`. A subject skipped because this lane cannot start its kind of package yet (OCI images, crates) was therefore never shown as our own gap, and nothing stopped a later change from putting it down to the server. Every skip now comes from `loop/skips.mjs` with a fault its reason allows (`SKIP_FAULTS` of the worker kit at 2ffcea1, which the workflows now pin): our limits (no runnable package, HTTP only, a fixture's HTTP init, incomplete sandbox evidence, no shard time left) are `tool`, the full write test of a third-party server and a subject outside the seed are `policy`. The driver writes no skip object of its own, and the pull-request proof checks that every bundle's skips declare a fault and that a no-package subject is `unassessed_tool`.

test.name: R-WC-24: every skip says its fault side, one the reason allows; our own limits are the tool's, never the subject's

records.title: Found by: review for R-WC-24.
records.description: Found by: review for R-WC-24. A harness error around a unit (a helper, the egress proxy, the bridge, Docker) was recorded as `upstream_unavailable`, the code for somebody else's outage, so our own failures read as a third party's. It is now `tool_error`, still retryable, with fault `tool`; the stages that ran before it are not skips.

test.name: R-WC-25: a harness error is our own tool_error (retryable), not somebody else's outage

records.title: Found by: review for R-WC-24.
records.description: Found by: review for R-WC-24. A failed install had no fault, and the obvious one (the subject's) is wrong whenever our environment stopped it. An install failure is now the subject's only when its own output shows a package-level error (npm E404, ETARGET or ENOVERSIONS, pip's no matching distribution or no satisfying version) or the package installed with nothing to run; our proxy refusing a host it asked for, our time limit, a kill at our memory limit (137) or timeout (124), a native build, or a failure with no evidence at all is `tool`. The install's own output is read only for these patterns and stays in `raw/`. Narrowed by R-WC-30 and R-WC-31 after the second review of #70.

test.name: R-WC-26: an install failure is the subject's only with a package-level error in its own output; our limits are the tool's

test.name: R-WC-28: the worker runs the commit the pump pins (tool_sha), checked whole, and stops unless the checkout is that commit

records.title: Found by: tool-qa#78 (R-PIN-01).
records.description: Found by: tool-qa#78 (R-PIN-01). The manifest reported `mcp-writecheck-action` at `GITHUB_SHA` (the head of the branch the YAML ran from, not necessarily the lane code that ran) and the sandbox as `mcp-surface-corpus-sandbox`, a name no pin uses, so `probe.mcp-surface-corpus` could never be proven. The driver now reports the commit checked out (`ACTION_SHA`, which must equal the checkout's HEAD) and names each tool by its pin key: `mcp-writecheck`, `mcp-writecheck-action`, `mcp-surface-corpus`, `gvisor`.

test.name: R-WC-29: the manifest names each tool by its tool-qa pin key, mcp-writecheck-action at the commit that ran

records.title: Found by: second review of #70.
records.description: Found by: second review of #70. Any failure of the install's entry step was put down to the subject, though msc's `sandbox/npm-entry.mjs` exits 1 for causes of ours too (a package.json it could not read, a bin name that comes from our seed or registry mapping, a bin it could not resolve inside the package), Docker, the image or a crash exit 125, 126, 127 or 139, and an entry step that exited 0 without a usable answer was blamed as well; the helper's answer was not even read, being kept out of the install log. The driver now passes that answer on as a code (`entryErrorCode`): only `declares_no_bin` (no bin, no main, no name asked for) is the subject's; every other code, any other exit code, and an entry failure without a code are `tool`.

test.name: R-WC-30: an entry step failure is the subject's only when the package declares nothing to run; every other entry answer is ours

records.title: Found by: second review of #70.
records.description: Found by: second review of #70. The install-log patterns could blame the server for our own trouble or be forged by it: pip prints "No matching distribution found" and "Could not find a version that satisfies" after its own connection retries, a proxy or DNS outage (which leaves no refused-host record) and when only our image's Python version is excluded; and with npm lifecycle scripts on, a package's script could print "npm error code E404" itself. Evidence now counts only where no code of the package could have written it: npm with scripts off, and only npm's final error block; pip only with "(from versions: none)" for the package itself, no build of anything, and no sign of retries, connections, name resolution or a Python-version filter. Everything else is `tool`.

test.name: R-WC-31: install output counts as evidence only where no code of the package could have written it, and only about the package
R-WC-26: an install failure is the subject's only with a package-level error in its own output; our limits are the tool's

records.title: Found by: design review of WC14 (OCI subjects).
records.description: Found by: design review of WC14 (OCI subjects). An OCI subject's server container is its own image, so neither our bridge nor the start command is ours to assume: the bridge (Node from the tools volume) would not start in a musl, distroless or scratch image, setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for it would leak into the server it spawns, and a guessed command would test some other program than the one `docker run` starts. The bridge now starts through the glibc loader and Node's libraries copied from our Node image into the tools volume (`rt/`, `--library-path` as a loader argument, no `LD_` variable), the driver refuses an OCI item when that runtime is missing, and the server command follows Docker's rules (entrypoint, then the entry's arguments or else the image's command; a replaced entrypoint drops the image's command), each part checked as one line of text, in the image's own working folder (an absolute path, else `/`). The server container mounts the read-only tools and nothing else of ours. Checked by hand on Alpine, BusyBox, distroless static and a Python Alpine image. The bridge is not a trust boundary: it runs inside the subject's own filesystem and sandbox, and only carries the server's stdio to the CLI, which runs in a container of its own (R-WC-05); the security review of #71 agreed.

test.name: R-WC-32: an OCI subject starts as docker run would start it, with the bridge through the portable runtime
R-WC-05: every subject and the forgery control run split; only our locked fixtures share the CLI's container

records.title: Found by: design review of WC14.
records.description: Found by: design review of WC14. A second resolver for OCI images in this lane would choose other images than the live-probe lane for the same subject, or run an image whose registry entry nobody verified. The lane now uses mcp-check's own `resolveSubject` (corpus/live-probe.mjs), fetched at `MCP_CHECK_REF`, the commit tool-qa's live-probe lane runs, and checked at load for every name it uses; a subject with no runnable image gets that resolver's own reason, retryability and fault side (`DETAILS`), and a rate limit or outage of a registry is retried, never replaced by a build.

test.name: R-WC-33: an OCI subject gets the image the live-probe resolver chooses, with its codes and fault sides when there is none
R-WC-33: with a checkout of mcp-check at MCP_CHECK_REF, its own resolver chooses the image from a registry entry

records.title: Found by: design review of WC14 (crates).
records.description: Found by: design review of WC14 (crates). Building a crate in the sandbox could resolve dependencies anew, reach hosts other than crates.io, leave gigabytes of build output in the volume the server's container mounts, or start the wrong one of several binaries. `cargo install --locked` (the Cargo.lock the crate published, when it published one; without one cargo warns and resolves afresh) runs in the Rust image pinned by digest in `loop/images.json` (a key of its own, never one of the sandbox's), as a build (`MS.build`), with only index.crates.io and static.crates.io on the proxy's list; `--` ends the options before the crate name, which is checked; the target folder and cargo home are removed before the server starts; and `cargo-entry.mjs` takes the binary from cargo's own record (`.crates2.json`, crates.io only): the only one, else the one named for the crate, else the only one named for MCP, never a guess between others, and only a regular file in `bin/`.

test.name: R-WC-34: a crate builds with its own lockfile in the pinned Rust image, through crates.io only, and leaves only its binary
R-WC-34: the crate's binary is the one cargo recorded, picked without a guess

records.title: Found by: design review of WC14.
records.description: Found by: design review of WC14. OCI images of up to 2 GB each would pile up on Docker's data root, a 20 GB filesystem of its own on the runner, over a shard of ten. A subject's image is now removed as soon as its unit's containers are gone, also when its pull failed half way (the reference is recorded before the pull).

test.name: R-WC-35: an OCI subject's image is removed when its unit ends, after its containers
R-WC-35: with a stand-in Docker, the subject's image is gone from the image list after its unit, also when the unit ends early

records.title: Found by: review for R-WC-26.
records.description: Found by: review for R-WC-26. An install that ended without a server to start would have been put down to the subject whatever the cause. Only the subject's own lack is its fault (an image with no command, a crate that installs no binary, a crate that is not on crates.io); a crate with several binaries and none named for it (we would have to guess), an image config we could not read, an image of another platform, an image that would not pull on a digest the resolver had just read, or a build failure is ours.

test.name: R-WC-36: an install that ended without a server to start is the subject's only for its own lack (no command, no binary)

records.title: Found by: security review of #71.
records.description: Found by: security review of #71. The bridge runs in the subject's image with that image's environment, so an image's NODE_OPTIONS, OPENSSL_CONF, GCONV_PATH or GLIBC_TUNABLES (or LD_PRELOAD, LD_AUDIT) reached our Node; one that stopped it gave "the server bridge did not start", a retryable harness error, so the subject was sent out again and again. The bridge now starts with those Node, OpenSSL and glibc variables emptied (an image that sets LD_PRELOAD or LD_AUDIT, which msc never lets a target's environment set or empty, is refused before it runs: `image_env_loader`, ours), the server gets the image's own environment back (Config.Env from inspect, with ours on top, passed to the bridge apart from its own), the reserved names (HOME, TMPDIR, SURFACE_SANDBOX) are always ours, and a bridge that does not start in an OCI image is `tool_error`, fault `tool`, not retryable. Not a trust boundary (R-WC-32).

test.name: R-WC-37: the bridge starts with the image's Node, OpenSSL and glibc variables emptied, the server gets the image's environment back, and a bridge that does not start is not retried

records.title: Found by: security review of #71.
records.description: Found by: security review of #71. The pull did not repeat live-probe's own checks (mcp-check R-LP-16), though the driver required their names: the image's host among mcp-check's OCI_HOSTS, its registry size within OCI_MAX_BYTES, and room on Docker's data root. They now run on what the resolver returned before the pull (another host, an unknown or too large size: ours; less than four times the image's size free: retryable, `infra`), and after the pull the unpacked size (`docker image inspect` .Size) must be within three times the cap.

test.name: R-WC-38: an OCI image is pulled only from an allowed host, within the size cap, with room on the data root; its unpacked size is capped too

records.title: Found by: security review of #71.
records.description: Found by: security review of #71. Each VOLUME path an image declares is a writable anonymous volume despite the read-only root, on the volumes filesystem the shard's other units share. The count is recorded, and an image that declares more than three is refused (`image_volumes`, ours, not retryable).

test.name: R-WC-39: an image that declares more VOLUME paths than a few is refused; the count is recorded

records.title: Found by: loop findings of 27 Nov (RUNNING-LANES finding 1).
records.description: Found by: loop findings of 27 Nov (RUNNING-LANES finding 1). A stage was marked as run whenever its step was attempted (`loop/run-items.mjs`), so a server whose init, plan and catalog all exited 4 ("server INIT did not initialize: timed out", no tool read) had no skip but the full stage's policy one and was published as fault `policy`, coverage `excluded`: 35 results of 25 and 26 Nov and 3 of 27 Nov over apollographql/apollo-mcp-server (its log: it could not read `/config.yaml`), grafana/mcp-grafana, tuananh/hyper-mcp, and isokron-ai/mcp-check, sea-lite and mcp-catalog-snap (npm packages that resolve to a command line tool). A stage now runs only when its step exits 0 or 1 (the CLI's `exitRanToCompletion`) inside our time limit (`stagesRan`); each of init, plan and catalog that did not run is a skip of ours, fault `tool`, with what stopped it in `logs/driver.json` `stage_detail` (`stageFailure`: `start_needs_config`, `not_a_server`, `step_timeout`, `cli_refused`, `start_failed`, `not_attempted`), never `subject` and never `policy`. The full stage of a fixture whose plan did not run is `tool_error` (tool), not policy, and a full write test that started and stopped gets a tool skip from `stageFailure` (review of #74). Mutation-checked: with attempts counted as runs again, or with the stage skip left out, the test fails.

test.name: R-WC-40: a stage counts as run only when its step ended with a status that means it ran; a server whose init, plan and catalog failed is ours, never excluded by policy

records.title: Found by: the t0-self lane, 28 Nov (selftest runs 46089149558 and 46090094104 failed on every dispatch, so each t0-self control was rejected as control_failed).
records.description: Found by: the t0-self lane, 28 Nov (selftest runs 46089149558 and 46090094104 failed on every dispatch, so each t0-self control was rejected as control_failed). selftest.yml runs every unit test with CI and CLI_DIR set, which makes the PostgreSQL fixture's live tests required (R-WC-17), but the job never installed the fixture's dependencies, and the test joined an absolute CLI_DIR under the working folder, so it could not find the CLI either. The test now resolves CLI_DIR, and selftest installs the fixture's dependencies from the committed lockfile (as test.yml's pg-fixture job does) before the local test.

test.name: R-WC-41: CLI_DIR is found whether it is absolute (selftest.yml) or relative (test.yml), and selftest installs the fixture before its required live tests

records.title: The T0 workers checked each dispatch input with `printf '%s' "$v" | grep -Eq`, which matches line by line: a value with a newline passed when one of its lines did, and its second line then went into …
records.description: The T0 workers checked each dispatch input with `printf '%s' "$v" | grep -Eq`, which matches line by line: a value with a newline passed when one of its lines did, and its second line then went into `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` as an output of its own (for example a forged `run_key`). Only someone who can dispatch the workflows could send one. The check is now a whole-string `[[ "$v" =~ $pattern ]]` match, in all eight workflows.

test.name: R-INP-01: every T0 worker refuses a dispatch input with a newline in it
R-INP-01: the old grep check let a newline through, so the test above can fail

records.title: Found by: review (the 0.4.0 fresh-eyes review).
records.description: Found by: review (the 0.4.0 fresh-eyes review). The integration pass read ENOTEMPTY or EEXIST from a new lease's rename as "a lease is there" on every platform, though its own comment said that holds on POSIX only. On Windows ENOTEMPTY can be a file held open, so a start retried five times and ended with a generic message instead of the clear Windows refusal. The reading is now POSIX only, through a platform seam that tests both.

test.name: R-TT-07: on Windows a new lease's ENOTEMPTY that lasts, with no lease there, is retried as a lost race (R-TT-09) and then a clear refusal
R-TT-07: on Windows a new lease's EPERM that lasts, with no lease there, is retried as a lost race (R-TT-09) and then a clear refusal

records.title: Found by: CI (the first Windows run of the 0.4.0 suite, Node 24).
records.description: Found by: CI (the first Windows run of the 0.4.0 suite, Node 24). A start that finds a lease it cannot read the owner file of judged it at once: no pid, a young folder, so "locked by another start", and it refused. On Windows a file in a folder that another start is opening or moving, or that a just-killed holder is still letting go of, can fail to open for a moment, and three starts racing over a killed holder's lease all read it that way in the same round: none started (exactly one must). The owner file is always written before a lease is renamed into place, so a failed read is a read that failed for now; the start reads again, up to four more times 40 ms apart, before judging. A lease that stays unreadable and young is still refused.

test.name: R-TT-08: a lease whose owner file cannot be read at the first look is read again before the start is judged (Windows: racing starts over a killed holder's lease all refused)

records.title: Found by: CI (the release PR's Windows run).
records.description: Found by: CI (the release PR's Windows run). On Windows a start that lost a race for the data-dir lease could report the Windows refusal ("could not rename its new lease ... EPERM; on Windows another process may have a file in it open") instead of looking again: its rename was refused because the winner's lease was there, and by the time it checked, the winner had moved that lease aside. No double holder, but a misleading message and an intermittent racing-starts test. Such a refusal now counts as a lost race while tries remain; only one that lasts to the last try is reported.

test.name: R-TT-09: on Windows a new lease's rename refused (EPERM) while a racing start's lease is moved aside: this start looks again and takes the lease

records.title: Found by: review of #45.
records.description: Found by: review of #45. The control layout picked its two ports one at a time and released each before tiny-tracker bound it: the two picks could repeat, and another process could take a port in between, failing the cell as a writecheck error. The ports are now picked together (always distinct), and a run whose server lost a picked port (EADDRINUSE) is retried on fresh ports, at most three times; any other failure is not retried.

test.name: R-DM-29: the control layout's ports are distinct, and a run whose server lost a picked port (EADDRINUSE) is retried on fresh ports, at most CONTROL_ATTEMPTS times (stub CLI)
